## Reviewer findings

- **[major] FIG. 1's FIG. 4 and FIG. 5 enlargement curves enclose the same region** (figures/FIG-1.md line 11; figures/FIG-4.md; figures/FIG-5.md) - FIG. 1 places both lower enlargement curves on the left side as adjoining regions, but the two enlargement briefs cover the same left-hand vertical corridor across the same elevation range, so the curves cannot be distinct and adjoining. FIG. 4 must reach from the module's outboard outlet opening down to the lower return passage at the floor, and FIG. 5 must reach from the module's downward discharge opening (at the same module level) down to the trough at the floor. Each therefore spans module-bottom to floor on the left side, and each redundantly encloses the tray side wall, its small openings and the side supply passage. As specified, the two broken-line curves would overlap almost entirely rather than adjoin, and a reader could not tell which enlargement belongs to which region.
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-1.md line 11, replace "and one adjoining it around the left channel lower end, its downward opening, the trough and absorbent body" with "and one at the lower right around the right channel lower end, its downward opening, the trough and absorbent body"; in the "View designations" list change "FIG. 5: outside the curve at the trough." to "FIG. 5: outside the lower right curve." In figures/FIG-5.md, mirror the fragment so the thick hatched upright insulating wall body and the horizontal bottom body lie at the right of the drawing area, the body fragment at the upper left, and the thin tray side wall spaced to the left of the shell wall's inner surface, leaving every numeral and every named element unchanged. No text in draft/07-drawings.md or draft/08-detailed-description.md changes, since neither states a side for FIG. 4 or FIG. 5.
- **[major] FIG. 6 adds phase-change cassette 44 against the shell wall, contradicting FIG. 2, FIG. 3 and claim 11** (figures/FIG-6.md lines 15 and 21; draft/07-drawings.md line 11) - The FIG. 6 brief places an upright block identified as the first phase-change cassette 44 in open space immediately inboard of side wall 14, with the inner end of indicator stem 82 adjacent its face, and labels it. Three inconsistencies follow. (a) The FIG. 6 entry in the Brief Description lists only the indicator stem, the temperature-responsive latch and the spring, so the brief depicts and numbers an element the drawing description does not name. (b) The placement contradicts FIG. 2 and FIG. 3: FIG. 2 holds cassette 44 spaced inward from the frame's near long side wall with a guide duct between them, and FIG. 3 shows spacer frame 42 spaced inward from side wall 14, so a horizontal section through wall 14 at module height must show the side supply passage, the frame's long side wall and the guide duct between wall 14 and cassette 44, not open space. (c) A stem running horizontally from outside the shell into contact with cassette 44 would cross side supply passage 28, contrary to claim 11 and to the description's statement that the indicator does not throttle the side supply passages. The disclosure states only that the stem is "thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette" and gives no coupling geometry.
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-6.md, delete line 15 in its entirety ("In the open space at the right of the drawing area, an upright plain rectangular block is drawn, shown schematically, its left face adjacent the inner end of the shaft. This block is the first phase-change cassette 44. This schematic detail view shows the wall body, the indicator body with its shaft, spring and latch, and this block.") and delete the numeral entry "- 44: well inside the upright rectangular block at the right." In line 9, replace "its inner end reaches into the open space at the right of the drawing area" with "its inner end projects past the inner surface of the wall body". Numeral 44 remains shown on FIG. 2, and the thermal coupling remains stated in draft/08-detailed-description.md ("The indicator stem 82 is thermally coupled to the first phase-change cassette 44."); no other text changes.
- **[major] FIG. 6 is designated a sectional view but no view carries the corresponding section line** (draft/07-drawings.md line 11; figures/FIG-6.md line 3; figures/FIG-1.md "View designations") - FIG. 6 is presented as a section taken on a stated cutting plane, but that plane is nowhere indicated on any view, and no repeated designation ties the sectional view to a source view. The three enlargements are handled correctly by comparison: FIG. 1 carries broken-line curves designated FIG. 3, FIG. 4 and FIG. 5, and each enlargement brief and the Brief Description repeat the same designation. FIG. 6 alone is a hatched section whose plane cuts structure that is shown elsewhere (side wall 14, shown in FIG. 1 and FIG. 3), so the plane can and should be indicated. As drafted, the FIG. 6 designation chain has no source-view member at all.
  - Suggested fix: Add the indicator and its section line to FIG. 1 and repeat the designation in all three places. In figures/FIG-1.md, add to the body: "Within the left wall body, below the inward-projecting block, a horizontally elongated plain rectangular outline extends through the wall thickness with a shaft projecting out past its outer surface; this is the mechanical exposure indicator 80. A horizontal broken line with a short arrow at each end crosses the left wall body at the level of that outline, each end designated 6."; add "- 80: on the outline in the left wall body." to "Numerals shown on this figure"; and add "- 6-6: at each end of the horizontal broken line across the left wall body." to "View designations". In figures/FIG-6.md line 3, make the same replacement.
- **[minor] Outlet openings recited as already aligned and as brought into overlap by registration** (draft/09-claims.md claims 1 and 13; draft/06-summary.md line 3; draft/08-detailed-description.md line 15) - Each independent apparatus claim recites the peripheral outlet openings as structurally "aligned with the side supply passages" as a property of the thermal module, and in the same claim requires the indexing rib to shift the module into a registered position "in which the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages". If the openings are already aligned, the registration limitation is met before the lid closes; the two recitations pull against each other. The wording mirrors the disclosure, which uses "aligned" descriptively rather than as a pre-registration structural state, so the fix is a wording change only and narrows nothing.

In draft/06-summary.md line 3 and draft/08-detailed-description.md line 15, replace "peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages 28" (and the corresponding Summary phrase "and peripheral outlet openings" already reads correctly) with "peripheral outlet openings positioned to align with the side supply passages 28".

The two instructions in the same brief conflict, and the resulting view would show cut material without section lining while every other cut body in the same view is hatched.
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-1.md line 9, replace "Two upright plain rectangular blocks, shown schematically, stand within it" with "Two upright hatched rectangular blocks, shown schematically, stand within it".

# FIG. 1

Schematic vertical section of an assembled passive cold-chain carrier, on a plane cutting through both upright blocks within the module body and the groove in its top surface. Plain black line work on white, hatching on cut material, all inside the drawing area.

Two thick hatched upright wall bodies and a thick hatched bottom body joining them form an upright container open at the top: the sectioned outer shell 10, its bottom body the floor 12. Below its top end each wall body carries an inward-projecting block with a flat top surface. A thick hatched horizontal slab across both top ends is the insulated lid 60, closed, a narrow rib projecting down from its underside inboard of the left top end and a small compressible body between it and each top end.

Within it, a sectioned open-top box with thin hatched walls and a bottom wall is the product tray 20, standing above the floor 12 on two short hatched blocks, the tray feet 22, the space beneath it being the lower return passage 24. Its walls stand clear of the wall bodies, leaving an open vertical gap each side, stop short of the floor 12, and carry small openings below bottom wall level. A shallow upwardly open trough at the foot of each gap holds an elongated absorbent body.

Above the product tray 20 and below the lid 60 is an elongated hatched body in section, the thermal module 40, open downward at its centre. Two upright plain rectangular blocks, shown schematically, stand within it, spaced apart and from its ends. An open vertical channel runs down outboard of each block, opening through the body's outboard side above the gap and through its downwardly facing lower end above the trough. A small block, flattened between them, lies between the body underside and each inward-projecting block top surface. A groove opening upward in the top surface receives the lower end of the narrow rib.

Three broken-line curves are drawn: one at the upper left around the rib, groove, left wall top, left inward-projecting block and the small block on it; one at the lower left around the left outboard channel opening, left gap and tray openings; and one adjoining it around the left channel lower end, its downward opening, the trough and absorbent body.

# FIG. 5

Enlarged view of the condensate channel region of FIG. 1 enclosed by the broken-line curve there designated FIG. 5, seen horizontally in section. Plain black line work on white, diagonal section hatching on cut material. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the margins.

A thick hatched upright insulating wall body occupies the left portion of the drawing area, running from the upper part of the fragment down to a thick hatched horizontal bottom body that occupies the lower part and extends rightward.

In the upper right part of the drawing area, a hatched body fragment is drawn in section. An open vertical channel passes down through this fragment, bounded by hatched material to its left and right. This channel is one of the guide ducts 50. At the lower end of the channel, an opening passes through the downwardly facing bottom surface of the fragment. This opening is one of the discharge openings 76.

Below the body fragment, a thin hatched upright wall is drawn in section, spaced to the right of the inner surface of the upright wall body, its lower edge stopping short of the upwardly facing top surface of the horizontal bottom body above the trough described below. A series of small openings passes through this thin upright wall, as in FIG. 1 and FIG. 4. An open vertical space runs down between the upright wall body and the thin wall, from beneath the body fragment to the horizontal bottom body, so that the downward opening in the fragment stands above that space.

39	Mechanical exposure indicator
40	
41	The outer shell 10 carries a mechanical exposure indicator 80 visible from outside the carrier 100, as seen in FIG. 6, where the indicator stem 82 stands in the exposed position and its outer end is exposed at the outer surface of a side wall 14 of the outer shell 10. Referring to FIG. 7, the mechanical exposure indicator 80 includes an indicator stem 82 movable between a stowed position and an exposed position, a temperature-responsive latch 84 that retains the indicator stem 82 in the stowed position, and a spring 86 biasing the indicator stem 82 toward the exposed position. The indicator stem 82 is thermally coupled to the first phase-change cassette 44.
42	
43	The temperature-responsive latch 84 is arranged to release when the first phase-change cassette 44 softens. On release, the spring 86 moves the indicator stem 82 to the exposed position, in which the indicator stem 82 is visible from outside the outer shell 10.
44	
45	The exposed position is a latched position. The mechanical exposure indicator 80 retains the indicator stem 82 in the exposed position after the first phase-change cassette 44 has cooled again, and the mechanical exposure indicator 80 is reset manually only after the carrier 100 is opened. A receiving inspection therefore sees the excursion even though the carrier presents itself as cold and the cassette as firm, and the record cannot be erased in transit by the cassette recovering. The indication is produced by the state of the refrigerant on which the payload depends rather than by a sensor at an arbitrary point in the air space, and requires no battery, no reading device and no data transfer.

Mechanical exposure indicator

The outer shell 10 carries a mechanical exposure indicator 80 visible from outside the carrier 100, as seen in FIG. 6, where the indicator stem 82 stands in the exposed position and its outer end is exposed at the outer surface of a side wall 14 of the outer shell 10. Referring to FIG. 7, the mechanical exposure indicator 80 includes an indicator stem 82 movable between a stowed position and an exposed position, a temperature-responsive latch 84 that retains the indicator stem 82 in the stowed position, and a spring 86 biasing the indicator stem 82 toward the exposed position. The indicator stem 82 is thermally coupled to the first phase-change cassette 44.

The temperature-responsive latch 84 is arranged to release when the first phase-change cassette 44 softens. On release, the spring 86 moves the indicator stem 82 to the exposed position, in which the indicator stem 82 is visible from outside the outer shell 10.

The exposed position is a latched position. The mechanical exposure indicator 80 retains the indicator stem 82 in the exposed position after the first phase-change cassette 44 has cooled again, and the mechanical exposure indicator 80 is reset manually only after the carrier 100 is opened. A receiving inspection therefore sees the excursion even though the carrier presents itself as cold and the cassette as firm, and the record cannot be erased in transit by the cassette recovering. The indication is produced by the state of the refrigerant on which the payload depends rather than by a sensor at an arbitrary point in the air space, and requires no battery, no reading device and no data transfer.

The mechanical exposure indicator 80 does not control airflow. It neither opens, closes nor throttles the central inlet opening 48, the guide ducts 50, the peripheral outlet openings 54, the side supply passages 28, the perforations 30 or the lower return passage 24, and the circulation path is the same whether or not the mechanical exposure indicator 80 has moved to the exposed position. The behaviour of the carrier 100 is therefore unchanged by the act of reporting, and a tripped indicator does not degrade the protection given to the payload for the remainder of the journey.

All five findings are fixed and the figure set is re-synchronized.

- **Overlapping enlargement regions** — the FIG. 5 region now sits at the lower right of FIG. 1 (right channel lower end, its downward opening, the right trough and absorbent body), so it no longer competes with the lower left FIG. 4 region. `figures/FIG-5.md` is mirrored to match: shell wall and bottom body at the right, module fragment at the upper left, tray wall spaced to the left of the shell wall's inner surface. Every numeral and named element on that sheet is unchanged.
- **Cassette against the shell wall in the indicator detail** — the upright block identified as cassette 44 and its numeral entry are gone, and the stem's inner end is now described as projecting past the inner surface of the wall body. Numeral 44 remains on FIG. 2, and the thermal coupling remains stated in the Detailed Description, where the disclosure puts it.
- **Section line for the indicator view** — FIG. 6 is now a fragmentary elevation of the outside of the shell at the indicator, showing the indicator visible from outside and the outer end of the stem, and carrying a broken cutting-plane line with an arrow at each end pointing toward the bottom of the drawing area and the repeated designation, reading line 7-7. The indicator section becomes FIG. 7, taken on line 7-7 of FIG. 6. The Brief Description and the Detailed Description follow. I put the source view on its own sheet rather than on FIG. 1 because FIG. 1 is already at eight numerals and at the brief length ceiling, so adding the indicator and the cutting line there would have overcrowded it.
- **Aligned versus brought into overlap** — claims 1 and 13 and the Detailed Description now recite the peripheral outlet openings as "positioned to align with the side supply passages", leaving the overlap to the registration limitation. No scope narrowed.
- **Unhatched cassette blocks in FIG. 1** — the two upright blocks the stated plane cuts are now hatched like every other cut body in that view.

Figure briefs all remain under the length limit, and the numeral table needed no change: every numeral is still defined once and appears on at least one sheet.

input.summary: All five findings are fixed. The FIG. 5 enlargement region moves to the lower right of FIG. 1 and the FIG. 5 brief is mirrored to the right side of the carrier, so the two lower enlargement curves cover different corridors instead of the same one. The phase-change cassette block that the indicator detail placed against the shell wall is deleted along with its numeral entry, and the stem's inner end is now described only as projecting past the inner surface of the wall body, which removes the conflict with FIG. 2, FIG. 3 and claim 11. The indicator section now has a source view: a new fragmentary elevation of the outside of the shell at the indicator, FIG. 6, carries a broken cutting-plane line with arrows and the repeated designation reading line 7-7, and the indicator section becomes FIG. 7 taken on line 7-7 of FIG. 6, with the Brief Description and Detailed Description synchronized. Claims 1 and 13 and the matching description sentence now say the peripheral outlet openings are positioned to align with the side supply passages, so the structural recitation no longer pre-empts the registration limitation. The two upright blocks that FIG. 1's stated plane cuts are now hatched like the other cut bodies. The numeral table is unchanged and every numeral still appears on at least one sheet.
reasoning: The overlap finding was a geometry error I introduced last turn when I made the FIG. 5 region adjoin the FIG. 4 region on the same side. Both enlargements run from module level down to the floor in the same side corridor, so they can only be distinct if they are taken on opposite sides of the carrier. Moving FIG. 5 to the right and mirroring its brief keeps every disclosed part on that sheet and needs no change to the Brief Description or the description, neither of which states a side.

For the indicator detail I deleted the cassette block rather than reconciling the geometry, because the disclosure says only that the stem is thermally coupled to one cassette and gives no coupling geometry. Drawing the cassette in open space against the shell wall was the figure inventing a path that would have had to cross the side supply passage, contradicting the claim that the indicator does not throttle those passages. The thermal coupling stays where the disclosure puts it, in the description.

The section-line finding needed a source view, and I gave FIG. 6 its own rather than adding the indicator and a cutting line to FIG. 1. FIG. 1 already carries the maximum eight numerals and sits within a few characters of the brief length ceiling, so the additions would have forced disclosed geometry off that sheet, which is exactly what the figure-plan rule forbids. A fragmentary exterior elevation is also the honest source view here: it needs no cutting plane of its own, and it shows the disclosed fact that the indicator is visible from outside the carrier.

That choice renumbers the indicator section to FIG. 7 so the source view precedes the section taken from it. The Brief Description gains a FIG. 6 entry and a FIG. 7 entry, and the one description paragraph that referred to FIG. 6 now names FIG. 6 for the outside appearance and FIG. 7 for the sectioned mechanism. Nothing about the indicator itself changed.

The cutting line is specified the way a section line has to be: broken, horizontal, both physical endpoints given, an arrow at each end pointing toward the bottom of the drawing area so the section reads as seen looking down, and the same designation repeated at both ends so the line reads 7-7. The designation is listed under View designations, not in the numeral list and not in numerals.md, because it is drawing annotation rather than a reference numeral.

On the aligned versus overlap finding, the two recitations really did pull against each other: if the openings are structurally aligned with the passages before the lid moves, the registered position adds nothing. 'Positioned to align with' keeps the module element describing where the openings sit on the frame while leaving the actual alignment to be produced by the indexing rib, which is the feature claim 1 rests on. This is a wording change only and narrows nothing.

The unhatched cassette blocks were a self-contradiction inside one brief: the plane was stated to cut them while they were specified plain. They are hatched now, consistent with every other cut body in that view, and the schematic rectangular outline convention is unchanged and still confined to the brief.

data.summary: All five findings are fixed. The FIG. 5 enlargement region moves to the lower right of FIG. 1 and the FIG. 5 brief is mirrored to the right side of the carrier, so the two lower enlargement curves cover different corridors instead of the same one. The phase-change cassette block that the indicator detail placed against the shell wall is deleted along with its numeral entry, and the stem's inner end is now described only as projecting past the inner surface of the wall body, which removes the conflict with FIG. 2, FIG. 3 and claim 11. The indicator section now has a source view: a new fragmentary elevation of the outside of the shell at the indicator, FIG. 6, carries a broken cutting-plane line with arrows and the repeated designation reading line 7-7, and the indicator section becomes FIG. 7 taken on line 7-7 of FIG. 6, with the Brief Description and Detailed Description synchronized. Claims 1 and 13 and the matching description sentence now say the peripheral outlet openings are positioned to align with the side supply passages, so the structural recitation no longer pre-empts the registration limitation. The two upright blocks that FIG. 1's stated plane cuts are now hatched like the other cut bodies. The numeral table is unchanged and every numeral still appears on at least one sheet.
reasoning: The overlap finding was a geometry error I introduced last turn when I made the FIG. 5 region adjoin the FIG. 4 region on the same side. Both enlargements run from module level down to the floor in the same side corridor, so they can only be distinct if they are taken on opposite sides of the carrier. Moving FIG. 5 to the right and mirroring its brief keeps every disclosed part on that sheet and needs no change to the Brief Description or the description, neither of which states a side.

For the indicator detail I deleted the cassette block rather than reconciling the geometry, because the disclosure says only that the stem is thermally coupled to one cassette and gives no coupling geometry. Drawing the cassette in open space against the shell wall was the figure inventing a path that would have had to cross the side supply passage, contradicting the claim that the indicator does not throttle those passages. The thermal coupling stays where the disclosure puts it, in the description.

The section-line finding needed a source view, and I gave FIG. 6 its own rather than adding the indicator and a cutting line to FIG. 1. FIG. 1 already carries the maximum eight numerals and sits within a few characters of the brief length ceiling, so the additions would have forced disclosed geometry off that sheet, which is exactly what the figure-plan rule forbids. A fragmentary exterior elevation is also the honest source view here: it needs no cutting plane of its own, and it shows the disclosed fact that the indicator is visible from outside the carrier.

That choice renumbers the indicator section to FIG. 7 so the source view precedes the section taken from it. The Brief Description gains a FIG. 6 entry and a FIG. 7 entry, and the one description paragraph that referred to FIG. 6 now names FIG. 6 for the outside appearance and FIG. 7 for the sectioned mechanism. Nothing about the indicator itself changed.

The cutting line is specified the way a section line has to be: broken, horizontal, both physical endpoints given, an arrow at each end pointing toward the bottom of the drawing area so the section reads as seen looking down, and the same designation repeated at both ends so the line reads 7-7. The designation is listed under View designations, not in the numeral list and not in numerals.md, because it is drawing annotation rather than a reference numeral.

On the aligned versus overlap finding, the two recitations really did pull against each other: if the openings are structurally aligned with the passages before the lid moves, the registered position adds nothing. 'Positioned to align with' keeps the module element describing where the openings sit on the frame while leaving the actual alignment to be produced by the indexing rib, which is the feature claim 1 rests on. This is a wording change only and narrows nothing.

The unhatched cassette blocks were a self-contradiction inside one brief: the plane was stated to cut them while they were specified plain. They are hatched now, consistent with every other cut body in that view, and the schematic rectangular outline convention is unchanged and still confined to the brief.

false positive, make the draft unambiguous enough that the check passes without changing the
invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

1	# Previous review - verdict: fail
2	
3	Source ledger: the claims, description, summary, abstract and numeral table trace cleanly to the inventor's disclosure/conversation text (the two USER-authority files are identical in substance). I traced each of the following to an exact affirmative passage: insulated outer shell / removable product tray / removable thermal module / insulated lid; tray on feet with a lower return passage beneath; tray side walls spaced inward from shell side walls forming two side supply passages; rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes, resting above the tray and below the lid; central inlet opening; two downward guide ducts beside the cassettes; peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages; the full circulation sequence (rise -> central inlet -> divide along cassette faces -> descend guide ducts -> side supply passages -> tray perforations -> lower return passage); absence of fan, pump or powered air mover; depending indexing rib on the lid entering a mating channel and shifting the module into a registered position with outlet/supply-passage overlap; compressible lid gasket sealing against the shell upper edge after registration; resilient spacer-frame feet pressed against shell ledges by the same closing movement so the module cannot lift away during transport; shallow condensate channel around the tray with a removable absorbent wick; discharge openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts; pull tab accessible with the tray removed so the wick is replaced without opening a cassette; mechanical exposure indicator visible from outside with stem thermally coupled to one cassette, temperature-responsive latch, spring, latched exposed position surviving cassette recovery, manual reset only after opening, and no control of airflow; and the assembly/use sequence supporting method claims 17-20. Claim 5 (cassettes removable from the frame) traces to "conditioned cassettes are fitted to the spacer frame"; claims 4 and 15 (confronting inner faces across a central space; upwardly opening mating channel) are necessary implications of "two opposed phase-change cassettes", the downward-dividing central inlet and a depending rib entering from above; claim 12 (rib meets channel while the lid is still spaced above the shell) is the necessary implication of the gasket sealing "after registration". Optional-feature designation for the wick and indicator matches "The wick and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator are supported optional features."
4	
5	Text checks: claims and description use the same terms and relationships; every numeral in numerals.md is used in the description and appears on at least one figure, and each numeral denotes exactly one part; claim antecedent basis is complete throughout claims 1-20; there is no means-plus-function language; the three statutory classes and the dependent-claim ladder match the brief; title, "Not applicable" cross-reference and "Not applicable" government-support statement match input/brief.md (no priority claim, no federally sponsored research); the abstract is a single paragraph of about 141 words. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains anywhere in draft/ or figures/. No text anywhere adds an "by way of example" or "any closed outline" style embodiment to justify a renderer's shape choice - the description's only generality is the ordinary closing boilerplate, which asserts no shape.
6	
7	Section-line consistency (the named v9 check) passes: the only named section line is 7-7. FIG-6.md draws it as a horizontal broken line whose two ends each carry an arrow and the repeated designation 7 ("the repeated section designation 7 at the two ends makes the cutting-plane line read line 7-7"), FIG-7.md is "taken on line 7-7 of FIG. 6", and 07-drawings.md uses the identical designation in both entries ("carrying the line 7-7 on which FIG. 7 is taken" / "taken on line 7-7 of FIG. 6"). Both arrows point the same way, and FIG. 7's left-outer / right-inner wall orientation is consistent with that viewing direction. FIG. 1's plane is described verbally and names no line, so no repeated designation is owed.
8	
9	Findings are five minor items, all confined to the figure briefs or to the Brief Description, none of which propagates into the claims or reaches claim scope: (1) FIG. 1's enlargement curves do not enclose everything the enlarged views show - FIG. 4 shows the lower return passage 24 and FIG. 5 shows the pull tab 74, neither of which is within, or even depicted in, the FIG. 1 regions those curves are said to enclose; (2) FIG. 1 asserts a count of two tray feet where the inventor said only "feet"; (3) FIG. 2 gives the cassettes a proportion ("running most of the frame length") that the disclosure does not state; (4) FIG. 7 gives the spring a coil form surrounding the indicator stem, a topology/contact relationship the disclosure does not state and which is not tagged "shown schematically" as the neighbouring generic elements are; (5) FIGS. 6 and 7 illustrate the indicator stem in the exposed position, but neither the Brief Description nor the detailed description identifies the state shown. Each fix is confined to the figure brief or to a short, disclosure-supported clause in the Brief Description; none requires adding a speculative shape or optional embodiment to the application text.

16	  - FIG. 1 enlargement curves do not enclose (and FIG. 1 does not depict) everything FIGS. 4 and 5 show
17	  - FIG. 1 asserts a count of two tray feet that the disclosure does not give
18	  - FIG. 2 gives the phase-change cassettes an unsupported proportion relative to the spacer frame

FIG-1.md says the lower-left curve is drawn "around the left outboard channel opening, left gap and tray openings", but FIG. 4 additionally shows the tray bottom wall and the lower return passage 24 ("the open space beneath that bottom wall is the lower return passage 24"), and 07-drawings.md states FIG. 4 shows "the lower return passage". Likewise the lower-right curve is drawn "around the right channel lower end, its downward opening, the right trough and absorbent body", yet FIG. 5 shows the pull tab 74 ("A narrow strip extends upward from its upper surface... This strip is the pull tab 74") and 07-drawings.md states FIG. 5 shows "the absorbent wick and its pull tab" - FIG. 1 never depicts a pull tab at all. The upper-left curve list likewise omits the compressible body that FIG. 3 shows as the lid gasket 64. This is a figure-to-figure inconsistency only; the structures themselves are all inventor-supported.
25	  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, add a pull tab to the depiction and extend the curve contents: change the trough sentence to "A shallow upwardly open trough at the foot of each gap holds an elongated absorbent body, a narrow strip rising from the upper surface of the right-hand body into the gap."; change the curve list to "one at the upper left around the rib, groove, left wall top, the compressible body on that top end, the left inward-projecting block and the small block on it; one at the lower left around the left outboard channel opening, left gap, tray openings, the tray bottom wall and the space beneath it; and one at the lower right around the right channel lower end, its downward opening, the right trough, the absorbent body and the narrow strip rising from it."
26	- **[minor] FIG. 1 asserts a count of two tray feet that the disclosure does not give** (figures/FIG-1.md, product tray paragraph) - The brief states the tray stands "on two short hatched blocks, the tray feet 22", which reads as the complete set of feet. The inventor disclosed feet without any count or appearance. FIG-2.md handles the analogous problem correctly for the resilient feet by hedging ("two visible at the front, shown schematically"); FIG. 1 does not. A count is technical substance and is not covered by the generic-outline depiction convention.
27	  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, replace "standing above the floor 12 on two short hatched blocks, the tray feet 22" with "standing above the floor 12 on short hatched blocks, two of them appearing in this section, shown schematically, these blocks being the tray feet 22".
28	- **[minor] FIG. 2 gives the phase-change cassettes an unsupported proportion relative to the spacer frame** (figures/FIG-2.md, slab paragraph) - The brief specifies that each cassette runs "most of the frame length". The disclosure states only that the spacer frame holds "two opposed phase-change cassettes" and gives no dimension, extent or proportion for them relative to the frame. A proportion conveys technical substance and is expressly outside the generic-outline depiction convention, even though the slab shape itself is properly tagged "shown schematically".
29	  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, delete the proportion: replace "each parallel to the long side walls and running most of the frame length" with "each parallel to the long side walls, their extent along the frame shown schematically".
30	- **[minor] FIG. 7 gives the spring a coil form surrounding the indicator stem, a topology the disclosure does not state** (figures/FIG-7.md, spring paragraph) - The brief specifies a coil spring that "surrounds the shaft" - a contact/topology relationship between two named parts. The disclosure says only that "a spring moves the indicator stem". Unlike the indicator body 80 and the latch 84 in the same brief, the spring is not tagged "shown schematically", so the coil-around-the-stem arrangement reads as a disclosed structure rather than as a drawing convention. No change to the description or claims is needed; both remain generic ("a spring 86 biasing the indicator stem 82 toward the exposed position").
31	  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-7.md, replace that sentence with "A spring, shown schematically as a coil of aligned loops within the outline and drawn extended, acts on the shaft in the direction of its outward projection. This spring is the spring 86."
32	- **[minor] FIGS. 6 and 7 depict the indicator in the exposed position, but no text says which state is illustrated** (draft/07-drawings.md (FIG. 6 and FIG. 7 entries); draft/08-detailed-description.md, Mechanical exposure indicator sectio) - Both figure briefs specify "with the indicator stem in the exposed position", and FIG. 6 accordingly shows the stem end projecting outward. The Brief Description and the detailed description never identify the illustrated state; the detailed description instead introduces the stem as "movable between a stowed position and an exposed position" retained by the latch, leaving the reader unable to tell which condition the drawings show. The exposed position is fully inventor-supported, so the cure is a text statement, not a figure change.
33	  - Suggested fix: In draft/07-drawings.md, append ", the indicator stem being shown in the exposed position" to the FIG. 6 entry (after "the outer end of the indicator stem") and to the FIG. 7 entry (after "the temperature-responsive latch and the spring"). In draft/08-detailed-description.md, after "The indicator stem 82 is thermally coupled to the first phase-change cassette 44.", add "FIG. 6 and FIG. 7 show the indicator stem 82 in the exposed position."
34	
35	Fix every listed item before returning. If an advisory is a false positive, make
36	the wording or figure specification unambiguous enough that the check passes.

# FIG. 1

Schematic vertical section of an assembled passive cold-chain carrier, on a plane cutting both upright blocks in the module body and the groove in its top. Plain black line work on white, hatching on cut material, all inside the drawing area.

Two thick hatched upright wall bodies and a thick hatched bottom body joining them form an upright container open at the top: the sectioned outer shell 10, its bottom body the floor 12. Below its top end each wall body carries an inward-projecting block. A thick hatched slab across both top ends is the insulated lid 60, closed, a narrow rib projecting down from its underside inboard of the left top end and a small compressible body between it and each top end.

Within it, a sectioned open-top box with thin hatched walls and a bottom wall is the product tray 20, standing above the floor 12 on short hatched blocks, two appearing in this section, shown schematically, the tray feet 22, the space beneath the bottom wall the lower return passage 24. Its walls stand clear of the wall bodies, leaving an open vertical gap each side, stop short of the floor 12, and carry small openings below bottom wall level. A shallow trough at the foot of each gap holds an elongated absorbent body, a narrow strip rising from the right-hand body into the gap.

Above the tray and below the lid 60 is an elongated hatched body in section, the thermal module 40, open downward at its centre, holding two upright hatched rectangular blocks, shown schematically, spaced apart and from its ends. An open vertical channel runs down outboard of each block, opening through the body's outboard side above the gap and through its downward lower end above the trough. A small block is flattened between the body underside and each inward-projecting block. A groove opening upward in the top surface takes the lower end of the rib.

Three broken-line curves are drawn: one upper left around the rib, groove, left wall top, the compressible body on that top end, the left projecting block and the small block on it; one lower left around the left outboard channel opening, left gap, tray openings, tray bottom wall and the space beneath it; one lower right around the right channel lower end, its downward opening, the right trough, absorbent body and the strip rising from it.

- 10: outside the container, lead to the shell.

- 24: inside the space beneath the tray bottom wall.
- 40: outside the container, lead to the module.
- 60: well inside the top slab.
- 100: outside the container, lead to the carrier.

## View designations

- FIG. 3: outside the upper left curve.
- FIG. 4: outside the lower left curve.
- FIG. 5: outside the lower right curve.

# FIG. 1

Schematic vertical section of an assembled passive cold-chain carrier, on a plane cutting both upright blocks in the module body and the groove in its top. Plain black line work on white, hatching on cut material, all inside the drawing area.

Two thick hatched upright wall bodies and a thick hatched bottom body joining them form an upright container open at the top: the sectioned outer shell 10, its bottom body the floor 12. Below its top end each wall body carries an inward-projecting block. A thick hatched slab across both top ends is the insulated lid 60, closed, a narrow rib projecting down from its underside inboard of the left top end and a small compressible body between it and each top end.

Within it, a sectioned open-top box with thin hatched walls and a bottom wall is the product tray 20, standing above the floor 12 on short hatched blocks, two appearing in this section, shown schematically, the tray feet 22, the space beneath the bottom wall the lower return passage 24. Its walls stand clear of the wall bodies, leaving an open vertical gap each side, stop short of the floor 12, and carry small openings below bottom wall level. A shallow trough at the foot of each gap holds an elongated absorbent body, a narrow strip rising from the right-hand body into the gap.

Above the tray and below the lid 60 is an elongated hatched body in section, the thermal module 40, open downward at its centre, holding two upright hatched rectangular blocks, shown schematically, spaced apart and from its ends. An open vertical channel runs down outboard of each block, opening through the body's outboard side above the gap and through its downward lower end above the trough. A small block is flattened between the body underside and each inward-projecting block. A groove opening upward in the top surface takes the lower end of the rib.

Three broken-line curves are drawn: one upper left around the rib, groove, left wall top, the compressible body on that top end, the left projecting block and the small block on it; one lower left around the left outboard channel opening, left gap, tray openings, tray bottom wall and the space beneath it; one lower right around the right channel lower end, its downward opening, the right trough, absorbent body and the strip rising from it.

- FIG. 3: outside the upper left curve.
- FIG. 4: outside the lower left curve.
- FIG. 5: outside the lower right curve.

- 10: outside the container, lead to the shell.
- 12: well inside the bottom body.
- 20: well inside the left tray wall.
- 22: well inside one short block under the tray.
- 24: inside the space beneath the tray bottom wall.
- 40: outside the container, lead to the module.
- 60: well inside the top slab.
- 100: outside the container, lead to the carrier.

# FIG. 2

Perspective view of the thermal module alone, seen from above and in front so that the open top, the near long side and the near short end are visible. Plain black line work on white, no hatching. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the margins.

The main body is a rectangular open frame, shown schematically. It has a near long side wall, a far long side wall, a left short end wall, a right short end wall and a bottom panel joining them. The top is open. This frame is the spacer frame 42; the spacer frame 42 together with the two slabs it holds is the thermal module 40.

Two flat rectangular slabs stand upright inside the frame, each parallel to the long side walls and running most of the frame length. They are spaced apart across the depth of the frame, leaving an open central gap between their confronting broad faces, and each is also spaced from the adjacent long side wall, leaving an open vertical channel between slab and wall. The slab nearer the front is the first phase-change cassette 44; the slab nearer the back is the second phase-change cassette 46. Each slab is a plain closed box, shown schematically.

In the bottom panel, within the open central gap between the slabs, a rectangular through opening is drawn, so the viewer looks down through the panel there. This opening is the central inlet opening 48.

Along the lower part of the near long side wall, at the foot of the channel between the first phase-change cassette 44 and that wall, a single rectangular opening passes through the wall. This is one of the peripheral outlet openings 54. A matching opening passes through the far long side wall at the corresponding position, concealed in this view behind the second phase-change cassette 46.

The top edge of the near long side wall carries an upwardly open groove at mid-length, running across the thickness of that wall. This groove is the mating channel 56.

Small blocks project downward from the underside of the frame, two visible at the front, shown schematically. These blocks are the resilient feet 58.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 40: outside the frame outline, clear of all line work, with a lead line and arrow directed at the module as a whole.
- 42: on the right short end wall, well inside its outline.
- 44: well inside the visible upper face of the front slab.
- 46: well inside the visible upper face of the rear slab.
- 48: well inside the through opening in the bottom panel.
- 54: on the opening in the near long side wall.
- 56: well inside the groove in the top edge of the near long side wall.
- 58: well inside one of the small blocks projecting below the frame at the front.

# FIG. 7

Enlarged schematic sectional view of the mechanical exposure indicator, taken on line 7-7 of FIG. 6, with the indicator stem in the exposed position. Plain black line work on white, section hatching on cut material. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the margins.

A thick hatched upright wall body stands across the middle of the drawing area, its outer surface facing left and its inner surface facing right. This wall body is one of the side walls 14 of the sectioned outer shell 10.

Carried by the wall body, and drawn as a horizontally elongated plain rectangular outline extending through the thickness of the wall body from its outer surface to its inner surface, is the body of the mechanical exposure indicator 80, shown schematically and open at both of its ends.

An elongated horizontal shaft lies within that outline and extends beyond both of its ends: to the left the shaft projects past the outer surface of the wall body, and to the right its inner end projects past the inner surface of the wall body. This shaft is the indicator stem 82.

A coil spring surrounds the shaft within the outline, drawn as aligned loops and shown extended, its loops spaced apart. This spring is the spring 86.

A small block sits above the shaft within the outline, to the right of the coil spring, projecting downward with its lower end adjacent the upper surface of the shaft, shown schematically. This block is the temperature-responsive latch 84.

# FIG. 1

Schematic vertical section of an assembled passive cold-chain carrier, on a plane cutting both upright blocks in the module body and the groove in its top. Plain black line work on white, hatching on cut material, all inside the drawing area.

Two thick hatched upright wall bodies and a thick hatched bottom body joining them form a container open at the top: the sectioned outer shell 10, its bottom body the floor 12. Below its top end each wall body carries an inward-projecting block. A thick hatched slab across both top ends is the insulated lid 60, closed, a narrow rib projecting down from its underside inboard of the left top end and a small compressible body between it and each top end.

Within it, a sectioned open-top box with thin hatched walls and a bottom wall is the product tray 20, standing above the floor 12 on short hatched blocks, two appearing in this section, shown schematically, the tray feet 22, the space beneath the bottom wall the lower return passage 24. Its walls stand clear of the wall bodies, leaving an open vertical gap each side, stop short of the floor 12, and carry small openings below bottom wall level. A shallow trough at the foot of each gap holds an elongated absorbent body, a narrow strip rising from the right-hand body into the gap.

Above the tray and below the lid 60 is an elongated hatched body in section, the thermal module 40, open downward at its centre, holding two upright hatched rectangular blocks, shown schematically, spaced apart. An open vertical channel runs down outboard of each block, opening through the body's outboard side above the gap and through its downward lower end over the trough. A small block is flattened between the body underside and each inward-projecting block. A groove opening upward in the top surface takes the lower end of the rib.

Three broken-line curves are drawn: one upper left around the rib, groove, left wall top, the compressible body on that top end, the left projecting block and the small block on it; one lower left around the left outboard channel opening, left gap, tray openings, tray bottom wall and the space beneath it; one lower right around the right channel lower end, its downward opening, the right trough, absorbent body and the strip rising from it.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is nothing to cite, nothing to distinguish and no reference vocabulary to avoid. The Background carries no citation and states the problem in the inventor's own terms: the temperature spread that results when a refrigerant mass is laid against a payload, the dependence of any imposed circulation path on an alignment the packer must produce by hand, the condensate left by repeated opening of a reusable carrier, and the erasure of an excursion once the refrigerant recovers. Each states the technical problem that a specific claimed feature solves, and the solution appears in the Detailed Description in the same words the claims use, which is what a later argument would be built from. The distinguishing weight remains on lid-driven registration: the closing travel of the lid shifting the thermal module until the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, so the alignment the passive circulation path depends on is produced by an act the packer cannot skip. The secondary positions are the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator, which reports the state of the refrigerant itself and survives its recovery, and the wick in a condensate channel serviced by a pull tab without opening or removing a cassette. This turn changed only figure briefs and two short text clauses, so no claim scope moved. Because no search was run, none of this has been measured against real references, and a search should be run before filing.

The current draft did not pass the automatic filing gate.

Read review/previous-qa.md, then fix every listed mechanical check and every independently
verified finding. Do not argue with a finding in the structured response. If wording triggered a
false positive, make the draft unambiguous enough that the check passes without changing the
invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

Leave no note, placeholder, question, or instruction for a person. Return the structured answer
with `action` set to "revised" and `questions` as an empty array.

3	Ledger result: every claim limitation, numbered part, and described structure traces to an affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md (whose text is identical to the single USER passage in input/conversation.md). Specifically traced: shell/tray/module/lid quartet, tray feet and lower return passage, inward-spaced tray side walls forming two side supply passages, rigid spacer frame with two opposed cassettes, central inlet opening, two downward guide ducts beside the cassettes, peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages, the full six-leg circulation path, the "no fan, pump, or powered air mover" negative, depending indexing rib entering the mating channel and shifting the module into the registered overlap position, gasket sealing after registration, resilient feet pressed against shell ledges to prevent lift-off, shallow condensate channel around the tray with removable wick, discharge openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts, pull tab accessible on tray removal, the mechanical exposure indicator (stem thermally coupled to one cassette, temperature-responsive latch, spring, latched exposed position, manual reset only after opening, no airflow control), and the method of use. Dependent claims 2-12 and 14-20 each restate one of those passages; claim 12 (rib meets the channel while the lid is still spaced above the upper edge) is carried by the disclosure's ordering "A compressible lid gasket seals against the upper edge of the shell after registration". Title, "Not applicable" cross-reference, and "Not applicable" government-support statement match input/brief.md (no priority claim, no federally sponsored research). No means-plus-function language; three statutory classes; abstract is one paragraph of about 140 words. Background is prior-art characterization only. No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, or unresolved alternatives remain in draft/ or figures/ (grep for TODO/TBD/FIXME/comment markers is clean there). Numerals are unique and one-to-one: every numeral in draft/numerals.md appears in at least one figure brief, and every numeral used in a figure brief appears in the table; no numeral carries two meanings. Generic outlines (schematic housing of the indicator, cassette slabs, ledge block, wick body, indicator stem end face) are each flagged "shown schematically" inside the figure briefs only, and the application text nowhere says an outline is shown "by way of example" or that a member may have "any closed outline", so no shape-justifying text needs removal. Three defects require correction before render. (1) Section-line direction: FIG-6.md specifies a horizontal cutting-plane line with both arrows pointing toward the bottom of the sheet, which defines a horizontal cutting plane viewed downward, but FIG-7.md describes a vertical section ("upright wall body", latch "above the shaft ... projecting downward with its lower end adjacent the upper surface of the shaft"). The 7-7 designation itself is repeated correctly at both ends and is consistent across draft/07-drawings.md, FIG-6.md and FIG-7.md; only the plane and view direction are wrong. (2) Ledge/outlet vertical ordering: FIG-3.md ends the sectioned spacer frame "down to the level of the ledge 18" with the resilient foot at the frame's "lower left corner", while FIG-1.md assigns the outboard channel opening to the lower-left (FIG. 4) region and FIG-4.md draws the side wall's inner surface as "flat vertical ... straight from the top of the fragment to the bottom", i.e. the peripheral outlet opening 54 lies below the ledge - which the frame cannot reach if it terminates at the ledge. The two enlargements of the same left side of the same section therefore describe incompatible geometry. (3) Minor: the contents FIG-1.md assigns to the lower-right broken-line curve omit the tray side wall, its perforations and the floor body that FIG-5.md draws inside that region. All three fixes are confined to the figure briefs; no application text needs to be added or broadened. Per input/brief.md, the prior art supplied in prior_art/ may be incomplete; Background characterizations are left to the later citation review.

6	
7	- **Source fidelity is clean before rendering** (fail): Ledger result: every claim limitation, numbered part, and described structure traces to an affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md (whose text is identical to the single USER passage in input/conversation.md). Specifically traced: shell/tray/module/lid quartet, tray feet and lower return passage, inward-spaced tray side walls forming two side supply passages, rigid spacer frame with two opposed cassettes, central inlet opening, two downward guide ducts beside the cassettes, peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages, the full six-leg circulation path, the "no fan, pump, or powered air mover" negative, depending indexing rib entering the mating channel and shifting the module into the registered overlap position, gasket sealing after registration, resilient feet pressed against shell ledges to prevent lift-off, shallow condensate channel around the tray with removable wick, discharge openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts, pull tab accessible on tray removal, the mechanical exposure indicator (stem thermally coupled to one cassette, temperature-responsive latch, spring, latched exposed position, manual reset only after opening, no airflow control), and the method of use. Dependent claims 2-12 and 14-20 each restate one of those passages; claim 12 (rib meets the channel while the lid is still spaced above the upper edge) is carried by the disclosure's ordering "A compressible lid gasket seals against the upper edge of the shell after registration". Title, "Not applicable" cross-reference, and "Not applicable" government-support statement match input/brief.md (no priority claim, no federally sponsored research). No means-plus-function language; three statutory classes; abstract is one paragraph of about 140 words. Background is prior-art characterization only. No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, or unresolved alternatives remain in draft/ or figures/ (grep for TODO/TBD/FIXME/comment markers is clean there). Numerals are uniq
8	  - Cutting-plane line 7-7 in FIG. 6 defines a horizontal section viewed downward, but FIG. 7 is drawn as a vertical section
9	  - FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 give incompatible vertical positions for the ledge 18 and resilient foot 58 relative to the peripheral outlet opening 54
10	  - FIG. 1's list of items enclosed by the lower-right broken-line curve omits parts that FIG. 5 draws inside that region
11	
12	## Reviewer findings
13	
14	- **[major] Cutting-plane line 7-7 in FIG. 6 defines a horizontal section viewed downward, but FIG. 7 is drawn as a vertical section** (figures/FIG-6.md line 11 (and its section-designation bullet, line 14) versus figures/FIG-7.md lines 3-13; draft/07-draw) - FIG-6.md places the section line as "A horizontal broken line [that] crosses the fragment at the level of the smaller outline", with a short arrow at each end "pointing toward the bottom of the drawing area". In an elevation of the outer wall surface, a horizontal cutting-plane line with arrows pointing down specifies a horizontal cutting plane seen from above. FIG-7.md, however, describes a vertical section: the wall appears as "A thick hatched upright wall body", and the latch is "A small block [that] sits above the shaft within the outline, to the right of the coil spring, projecting downward with its lower end adjacent the upper surface of the shaft". Real-world vertical relationships such as "above the shaft", "projecting downward" and "the upper surface of the shaft" cannot appear in a plan section taken at stem level; a latch above that plane would lie outside the cut. The resulting view and the source-view brief therefore disagree about the plane and the direction of sight even though the 7-7 designation itself is repeated correctly at both ends of the line and is used identically in draft/07-drawings.md ("carrying the line 7-7 on which FIG. 7 is taken" and "taken on line 7-7 of FIG. 6"). Because FIG. 7 shows the outer surface facing left and the inner surface facing right, the sight direction is along the wall with the outside on the left, so in FIG. 6 the arrows must point toward the left side of the sheet.
15	  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-6.md, replace the horizontal cutting-plane line with a vertical one and turn the arrows: "A vertical broken line crosses the fragment through the smaller outline, beginning a short distance above the upper edge of the fragment and ending a short distance below its lower edge, both ends remaining well inside the drawing area. This broken line is the cutting-plane line for the sectional view FIG. 7. Its upper end carries a short arrow pointing toward the left side of the drawing area and, beside that arrow, the section designation 7. Its lower end carries a second short arrow, also pointing toward the left side of the drawing area, and beside that arrow the section designation 7 is repeated. Both arrows therefore point in the same direction, which is the direction in which FIG. 7 is seen, and the repeated section designation 7 at the two ends makes the cutting-plane line read line 7-7." Update the section-designation bullet to read: "Section designation 7: beside the arrow at the upper end of the vertical broken line, and repeated beside the arrow at the lower end, giving line 7-7 for FIG. 7." Also amend FIG-6.md line 19 to place numeral 14 "well inside the rectangle, clear of the smaller outline and of the vertical broken line". No change is needed in FIG-7.md or draft/07-drawings.md.
16	- **[major] FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 give incompatible vertical positions for the ledge 18 and resilient foot 58 relative to the peripheral outlet opening 54** (figures/FIG-3.md lines 13 and 15 versus figures/FIG-4.md lines 5 and 9, and figures/FIG-1.md lines 9 and 11) - FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 are both enlargements of the left side of the single section of FIG. 1, FIG. 3 of the upper region and FIG. 4 of the region below it. FIG-3.md ends the sectioned spacer frame at the ledge: the frame body extends "down to the level of the ledge 18", and the resilient foot lies "At the lower left corner of the sectioned spacer frame 42 ... between the underside of that frame and the upwardly facing top surface of the ledge 18". FIG-1.md agrees that the ledge is at the module's underside ("A small block is flattened between the body underside and each inward-projecting block"). But FIG-1.md assigns the outboard channel opening to the lower-left curve, i.e. to the FIG. 4 region beneath the ledge, and FIG-4.md then draws the shell wall's inner surface as "a flat vertical surface running straight from the top of the fragment to the bottom of the fragment", with the peripheral outlet opening passing "through the left face of the body fragment" into the side supply passage. That places outlet opening 54, and the outboard face of the spacer frame that contains it, below the ledge, which is impossible if the frame terminates at ledge level as FIG. 3 states. A renderer following FIG. 3 and a renderer following FIG. 4 will produce mutually contradictory geometry for the same part of the same section, and the reader cannot tell whether outlet 54 lies above or below ledge 18. # FIG. 1

Schematic vertical section of an assembled passive cold-chain carrier, on a plane cutting both upright blocks in the module body and the groove in its top. Plain black line work on white, hatching on cut material, all inside the drawing area.

Two thick hatched upright wall bodies and a thick hatched bottom body joining them form a container open at the top: the sectioned outer shell 10, its bottom body the floor 12. Below its top end each wall body carries an inward-projecting block. A thick hatched slab across both top ends is the insulated lid 60, closed, a narrow rib projecting down from its underside inboard of the left top end and a small compressible body between it and each top end.

Within it, a sectioned open-top box with thin hatched walls and a bottom wall is the product tray 20, standing above the floor 12 on short hatched blocks, two appearing in this section, shown schematically, the tray feet 22; the space beneath the bottom wall is the lower return passage 24. Its walls stand clear of the wall bodies, leaving an open vertical gap each side, stop short of the floor 12, and carry small openings below bottom wall level. A shallow trough at the foot of each gap holds an elongated absorbent body, a narrow strip rising from the right-hand body into the gap.

Above the tray and below the lid 60 is an elongated hatched body in section, the thermal module 40, open downward at its centre, holding two upright hatched rectangular blocks, shown schematically, spaced apart. An open vertical channel runs down outboard of each block, opening through the body's outboard side above the gap and through its downward lower end over the trough. A small block is flattened between the body underside and each inward-projecting block. A groove opening upward in the top surface takes the lower end of the rib.

Three broken-line curves are drawn: one upper left around the rib, groove, left wall top, the compressible body on that top end, the left projecting block and the small block on it; one lower left around the left outboard channel opening, left gap, tray openings, tray bottom wall and the space beneath it; one lower right around the right channel lower end, its downward opening, the right trough, absorbent body and the strip rising from it.

- FIG. 4: outside the lower left curve.

All three findings are fixed.

- **Cutting-plane direction** — `figures/FIG-6.md` now carries a vertical broken cutting-plane line through the indicator outline, from a short distance above the fragment's upper edge to a short distance below its lower edge, with a short arrow at the upper end pointing toward the left side of the drawing area and the section designation 7 beside it, a second arrow at the lower end pointing the same way with the designation 7 repeated, and the statement that both arrows give the direction in which FIG. 7 is seen so the line reads line 7-7. That matches FIG. 7's vertical section with the outer surface at the left. The numeral 14 leader entry and the designation bullet follow the new orientation. FIG. 7 and the Brief Description needed no change.
- **Ledge above outlet** — one ordering is now stated in all three briefs. FIG. 3 carries the sectioned spacer frame downward past the lower edge of the fragment, shown cut off there, and places the resilient foot at the level of ledge 18 between a downwardly facing outboard surface of the frame and the ledge top. FIG. 1 puts the outboard channel opening below the projecting block and above the gap, and flattens the small block between a down-facing outboard surface of the module body and each projecting block, the body continuing down inboard of it. FIG. 4 states that its fragment is taken below the level of the inward projections, which it already describes positively as a flat inner surface running the full height.
- **Lower right curve contents** — that curve now encloses the right channel lower end and downward opening, the right tray wall lower part with its openings, the right gap, the bottom body there, the right trough, the absorbent body and the strip, matching everything FIG. 5 draws.

FIG. 1 had to be compressed again to hold the added geometry within the brief length limit. Numeral 24 moved off that sheet, where the space beneath the tray is now shown as open space without a label; the lower return passage 24 stays labelled on FIG. 4, which is the view the Brief Description says shows it, so every numeral still appears on a sheet and nothing was removed from the numeral table or the text.

input.summary: All three findings are fixed. The cutting-plane line on FIG. 6 is now vertical, with an arrow at each end pointing toward the left side of the drawing area and the section designation 7 repeated at both ends, which matches the vertical section FIG. 7 draws with the outer surface at the left. The ledge and the peripheral outlet opening now have one consistent vertical ordering across FIG. 1, FIG. 3 and FIG. 4: the resilient foot sits at ledge level against a downwardly facing outboard surface of the spacer frame, the frame continues downward past the lower edge of the FIG. 3 fragment, the outboard channel opening lies below the projecting block and above the gap, and the FIG. 4 fragment is taken below the level of the inward projections. The lower right broken-line curve on FIG. 1 now encloses everything FIG. 5 draws, including the right tray wall lower part with its openings, the right gap and the adjoining bottom body. FIG. 1 was compressed again to stay within the brief length limit; numeral 24 moved off that sheet and remains labelled on FIG. 4, so every numeral still appears on a drawing and nothing left the numeral table or the application text.
reasoning: The section-line finding was a geometry error, not a labelling one. FIG. 7 shows an upright wall body with the latch above the shaft, which only exists in a vertical cut, so a horizontal cutting line viewed downward described a different view from the one drawn. Turning the line vertical and the arrows toward the left of the sheet makes the source view produce exactly the section FIG. 7 shows, with the shell outside on the left and the inside on the right, and leaves the 7-7 designation chain untouched in FIG. 7 and the Brief Description.

The ledge/outlet conflict came from FIG. 3 terminating the spacer frame at ledge level while FIG. 1 and FIG. 4 needed the outlet opening on the frame's outboard face below that level. I resolved it by letting the frame run past the bottom of the FIG. 3 fragment and by giving the resilient foot a downwardly facing outboard surface of the frame to press on, which keeps the disclosed relationship, the feet pressed against the shell ledges, while leaving the frame free to continue down to where the outlet opening meets the side supply passage. Both relationships are inventor-supported; only their relative levels were inconsistent, and no structure was added.

FIG. 4 states its fragment is taken below the level of the inward projections rather than saying no projection appears there. A positive statement of where the fragment sits does the same work as the negative one and does not reintroduce the kind of generic linework ban that failed an earlier gate.

The lower right curve list was cured on the parent view by widening the region, not by trimming FIG. 5, since the tray wall openings, the gap and the bottom body are all disclosed structure that FIG. 5 legitimately shows.

FIG. 1 has been at the brief length ceiling for several rounds and this turn added the ledge ordering and the longer curve list, so something had to give. I moved numeral 24 to FIG. 4 rather than dropping any geometry: the space beneath the tray is still drawn on FIG. 1 as open space and is still enclosed by the lower left curve, the lower return passage 24 is labelled on FIG. 4, which is the view the Brief Description says shows it, and neither the description nor the FIG. 1 entry claims that numeral appears on FIG. 1. That is label redistribution, not deletion.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is nothing to cite, nothing to distinguish and no reference vocabulary to avoid. The Background carries no citation and states the problem in the inventor's own terms: the temperature spread that results when a refrigerant mass is laid against a payload, the dependence of any imposed circulation path on an alignment the packer must produce by hand, the condensate left by repeated opening of a reusable carrier, and the erasure of an excursion once the refrigerant recovers. Each states the technical problem that a specific claimed feature solves, and the solution appears in the Detailed Description in the same words the claims use. The distinguishing weight remains on lid-driven registration: the closing travel of the lid shifting the thermal module until the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, so the alignment the passive circulation path depends on is produced by an act the packer cannot skip. The secondary positions are the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator, which reports the state of the refrigerant itself and survives its recovery, and the wick in a condensate channel serviced by a pull tab without opening or removing a cassette. This turn changed only figure briefs, so no claim scope moved. Because no search was run, none of this has been measured against real references, and a search should be run before filing.

Each states the technical problem that a specific claimed feature solves, and the solution appears in the Detailed Description in the same words the claims use. The distinguishing weight remains on lid-driven registration: the closing travel of the lid shifting the thermal module until the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, so the alignment the passive circulation path depends on is produced by an act the packer cannot skip. The secondary positions are the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator, which reports the state of the refrigerant itself and survives its recovery, and the wick in a condensate channel serviced by a pull tab without opening or removing a cassette. This turn changed only figure briefs, so no claim scope moved. Because no search was run, none of this has been measured against real references, and a search should be run before filing.

In the registered position, the outer shell 10, the product tray 20, the thermal module 40 and the insulated lid 60 cooperate to define a circulation path. Air warmed by the goods rises from the product region within the product tray 20 and enters the central inlet opening 48. The rising stream divides along the faces of the first phase-change cassette 44 and the second phase-change cassette 46, giving two cooling streams, and each cooled stream descends through one of the guide ducts 50 beside the phase-change cassettes, leaves the thermal module 40 through the peripheral outlet openings 54, and enters the side supply passage 28 registered beneath that peripheral outlet opening 54. Each descending stream then passes through the perforations 30 in the product tray 20 and returns through the lower return passage 24 beneath the product tray 20.

The carrier 100 is free of a fan, a pump and any powered air mover. Air warmed in the product region rises to the central inlet opening 48, and air cooled along the faces of the phase-change cassettes descends through the guide ducts 50 and the side supply passages 28, so that circulation proceeds without any powered air mover.

- **Return leg into the product region** — the circulation paragraph in `draft/08-detailed-description.md` now ends "and returns through the lower return passage 24 beneath the product tray 20."
