lines: Registration and retention by the lid

-The insulated lid 60 carries a depending indexing rib 62 on an underside of the insulated lid 60, and a compressible lid gasket 64 carried on the underside of the insulated lid 60 and positioned to bear against the upper edge of the outer shell 10. The depending indexing rib 62, the mating channel 56 of the spacer frame 42 and the compressible lid gasket 64 are seen in FIG. 3. As the insulated lid 60 is closed, the depending indexing rib 62 enters the mating channel 56 of the spacer frame 42 and shifts the thermal module 40 into a registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings 54 overlap the side supply passages 28. The engagement is progressive: the depending indexing rib 62 first meets the mating channel 56 while the lid is still spaced above the outer shell 10, and the remaining closing travel translates the spacer frame 42 horizontally until the mating channel 56 is seated on the depending indexing rib 62.

+The insulated lid 60 carries a depending indexing rib 62 on an underside of the insulated lid 60, and a compressible lid gasket 64 carried on the underside of the insulated lid 60 and positioned to bear against the upper edge of the outer shell 10. The depending indexing rib 62, the mating channel 56 of the spacer frame 42 and the compressible lid gasket 64 are seen in FIG. 3. As the insulated lid 60 is closed, the depending indexing rib 62 enters the mating channel 56 of the spacer frame 42 and shifts the thermal module 40 into a registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings 54 overlap the side supply passages 28. The engagement is progressive: the depending indexing rib 62 first meets the mating channel 56 while the lid is still spaced above the outer shell 10, and the remaining closing travel translates the spacer frame 42 horizontally into the registered position.

This sequence addresses the practical problem that the circulation path depends on an alignment which a person packing quickly at a bench cannot be relied upon to produce. The thermal module 40 is placed in the outer shell 10 above the product tray 20, and the registration is completed by the closing of the lid. The alignment on which the circulation path depends is therefore created by an act the packer cannot omit, because a carrier that is not closed does not ship. The compressible lid gasket 64 bears against the upper edge of the outer shell 10 and is compressed only at the end of the closing travel, after the depending indexing rib 62 has completed registration, so that the carrier cannot be sealed shut around a thermal module 40 that is still out of position.

content:
The current draft did not pass the automatic filing gate.

Read review/previous-qa.md, then fix every listed mechanical check and every independently
verified finding. Do not argue with a finding in the structured response. If wording triggered a
false positive, make the draft unambiguous enough that the check passes without changing the
invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

Leave no note, placeholder, question, or instruction for a person. Return the structured answer
with `action` set to "revised" and `questions` as an empty array.

lines: This sequence addresses the practical problem that the circulation path depends on an alignment which a person packing quickly at a bench cannot be relied upon to produce. The thermal module 40 is placed in the outer shell 10 above the product tray 20, and the registration is completed by the closing of the lid. The alignment on which the circulation path depends is therefore created by an act the packer cannot omit, because a carrier that is not closed does not ship. The compressible lid gasket 64 bears against the upper edge of the outer shell 10 and is compressed only at the end of the closing travel, after the depending indexing rib 62 has completed registration, so that the carrier cannot be sealed shut around a thermal module 40 that is still out of position.

-The same closing movement retains the thermal module 40. Ledges 18 of the outer shell 10 lie beneath the resilient feet 58 of the spacer frame 42, as seen in FIG. 3, and closure of the insulated lid 60 presses the resilient feet 58 against the ledges 18. The resilient feet 58 are compressed between the ledges 18 and the load path from the insulated lid 60, so that the thermal module 40 is held down and cannot lift away from the product tray 20 during transport. The resilient feet 58 maintain a downward holding force during transport, so the registered overlap between the peripheral outlet openings 54 and the side supply passages 28 that was established at closure persists through the journey.

All six findings are fixed.

- **Mating channel runout** — `figures/FIG-2.md` now reads "The top edge of the near long side wall carries an upwardly open groove, shown schematically." No length direction is stated, so the brief no longer fixes a direction of constraint for the indexing rib.
- **Latch topology in FIG. 7** — the paragraph is now "A small block within the outline beside the shaft, shown schematically, is spaced from the shaft, the latch being shown released." The side of the stem, the order relative to the spring and the projection direction are gone, and the leader for 84 targets the block beside the shaft.
- **Indicator body and stem** — the body is now an outline within the outer portion of the wall body, open at its outer end, and the stem lies within it and projects to the left past the outer surface. No through-breach of the insulated wall and no inboard projection remain. The leader for 82 still points at the outwardly projecting part.
- **Foot bearing surface height** — the outward step now simply has "a downwardly facing surface outboard of the frame", with no level relationship to the bottom panel. The two following sentences and numeral 58 are unchanged.
- **Wick and tab detail** — FIG. 5 now has the absorbent body lying in the trough, shown schematically, and a narrow strip extending from one end of it with its free end clear of the body; the leader for 74 matches, and FIG. 1 now says only "a narrow strip at one end of the right-hand appearance".
- **"Load path" sentence** — the Detailed Description now reads "Closure of the insulated lid 60 compresses the resilient feet 58 between the spacer frame 42 and the ledges 18, so that the thermal module 40 is held down and cannot lift away from the product tray 20 during transport."

Numeral coverage still matches the table exactly in both directions, per-sheet counts are 7, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4 and 6, all briefs are within the length limit, and no placeholder or em dash remains. The claims and numeral table were not touched.

The indicator body in FIG. 7 now sits within the outer portion of the wall body, open at its outer end, with the stem lying inside it and projecting only outward, so no through-breach of the insulated wall and no inboard projection remain. The FIG. 2 outward step now has simply a downwardly facing surface outboard of the frame, with no level relationship to the bottom panel. The FIG. 5 wick lies in the trough with no fill depth and the pull tab extends from one end of it with its free end clear of the body, matched in FIG. 1 and in the leader for 74. In the Detailed Description the resilient feet are now compressed by closure of the lid between the spacer frame and the ledges, replacing the load-path wording. Numeral coverage still matches the table exactly in both directions, per-sheet counts are 7, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4 and 6, every brief is within the length limit, and the claims and numeral table are untouched.
reasoning: The two critical items were both cases of a brief settling a functional joint the inventor left open. A groove's runout direction decides which way the rib constrains the frame, and the latch's side, order and projection direction decide what face it acts on and where along the stem. Neither is in the source, so both had to come out rather than be softened, and both parts remain visible as simple outlines so the sheets still show the disclosed relationship.

For the indicator I kept only what the disclosure gives: the stem is visible from outside and moves to an exposed position. Running the body through the full wall thickness and pushing the stem past the inner surface added a breach of the insulation and a member reaching into the interior across the side supply passage, neither of which the source states. Thermal coupling stays where the inventor put it, as a functional statement in the description, with no geometry attached.

The step's bearing surface stays outboard, which the disclosure requires because feet of the frame must reach ledges projecting inward from the shell wall, but its height above the frame bottom is gone. That was the one part of the sentence with no source, and removing it does not disturb the retention relationship recited in claims 2, 14 and 18.

The wick and tab edits are small but the reasoning is the same: the trough is a flow boundary and the tab is the disclosed means of access, so fill depth and an in-trough end position are substance, not outline. The tab remains a strip extending from one end of the wick, which is what keeps it reachable when the tray is out.

The load-path sentence was indefinite on its face, since nothing can be compressed between a ledge and a path. Naming the spacer frame as the member that bears down is supported directly, because the disclosure says the closing movement presses the resilient feet of the spacer frame against the ledges of the shell, and it matches claim 2 without adding structure.
Every edit shortened its file, so no compensating compression was needed anywhere, and no numeral, leader target or curve content had to move.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is nothing to cite, nothing to distinguish and no reference vocabulary to avoid; the Background carries no citation and there is no characterisation for a citation review to test. The Background states the problem in the inventor's own terms: the temperature spread that results when a refrigerant mass is laid against a payload, the dependence of any imposed circulation path on an alignment the packer must produce by hand, the condensate left by repeated opening of a reusable carrier, and the erasure of an excursion once the refrigerant recovers. Each states the technical problem that a specific claimed feature solves, and the solution appears in the Detailed Description in the same words the claims use, which is what a later argument would be built from. The distinguishing weight remains on lid-driven registration: the closing travel of the lid shifting the thermal module until the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, so the alignment the passive circulation path depends on is produced by an act the packer cannot skip. The secondary positions are the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator, which reports the state of the refrigerant itself and survives its recovery, and the wick in a condensate channel serviced by a pull tab without opening or removing a cassette. This turn removed undisclosed joint geometry from four briefs and cured one indefinite sentence in the description, so no claim scope moved. As the drafting brief records, no prior-art search was run, so the claims have never been measured against a real reference and a search should be run before filing.

The current draft did not pass the automatic filing gate.

Read review/previous-qa.md, then fix every listed mechanical check and every independently
verified finding. Do not argue with a finding in the structured response. If wording triggered a
false positive, make the draft unambiguous enough that the check passes without changing the
invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

Leave no note, placeholder, question, or instruction for a person. Return the structured answer
with `action` set to "revised" and `questions` as an empty array.

The Background states the problem in the inventor's own terms: the temperature spread that results when a refrigerant mass is laid against a payload, the dependence of any imposed circulation path on an alignment the packer must produce by hand, the condensate left by repeated opening of a reusable carrier, and the erasure of an excursion once the refrigerant recovers. This turn deleted one undisclosed qualifier from a figure brief, so no claim scope moved. As the drafting brief records, no prior-art search was run, so the claims have never been measured against a real reference and a search should be run before filing.

All four findings are fixed.

- **Plural parts cited to single-instance enlargements** — the Detailed Description now reads "two downward guide ducts 50, one of which is seen in FIG. 4", "One tray side wall 26, one side supply passage 28 and the perforations 30 are seen in FIG. 4.", and "one such ledge 18 and one such resilient foot 58 being seen in FIG. 3". Each now matches what the cited brief actually places on the sheet, in the same style the draft already used for FIG. 5.
- **FIG. 2 view statement** — the view sentence now reads "so the open top, the near long side wall and the right short end wall are visible", which uses the wall names the brief goes on to define and makes the leader for 42 on the right short end wall consistent with the stated viewpoint.
- **FIG. 6 break lines** — all four edges of the wall fragment are now drawn as break lines, showing that the wall continues beyond the fragment on every side, so no edge reads as an actual end of the shell side wall and the brief asserts nothing about wall extent or indicator position along it.
- **Indefinite rib reference** — the mating channel paragraph now reads "The mating channel 56 and the depending indexing rib 62 described below, which enters it from above, are shaped so that...", giving the part its one designation throughout.

Verification after the edits: numerals across the seven sheets still match the 31 table entries exactly in both directions, every brief is within the length limit with FIG. 4 longest at 2798 characters, and no placeholder or em dash remains. The claims, the Brief Description and the numeral table were not touched.

input.summary: All four findings are fixed. Three sentences in the Detailed Description now cite the enlargements for what those sheets actually show: one of the two guide ducts 50 in FIG. 4, one tray side wall 26 with one side supply passage 28 and the perforations 30 in FIG. 4, and one ledge 18 with one resilient foot 58 in FIG. 3. The FIG. 2 view sentence now names the open top, the near long side wall and the right short end wall, which are the walls the brief defines and which makes the leader for 42 consistent with the viewpoint. The FIG. 6 wall fragment now has break lines on all four edges, so no edge reads as an actual end of the shell side wall. The mating channel paragraph now names the depending indexing rib 62 instead of an indefinite unnumbered rib. Numerals across the seven sheets still match the 31 table entries exactly in both directions, every brief is within the length limit with FIG. 4 longest at 2798 characters, and the claims, Brief Description and numeral table were not touched.
reasoning: The plural citations were a real mismatch between text and sheet, not a style quibble. FIG. 4 is a one-sided enlargement and FIG. 3 shows a single foot on a single ledge, so telling the examiner that the tray side walls, the guide ducts or the feet are seen there overstates what is on the page. Counting them down to what each brief places keeps the parts plural where the invention is plural, in the structural sentences and the claims, and accurate where the reference is to a drawing.

The FIG. 2 view sentence named a face the brief never defined. The frame has near and far long side walls and left and right short end walls, so a near short end is not one of them, and the leader for 42 depends on the right short end wall being in view. Naming that wall in the view sentence ties the viewpoint and the leader together without changing the frame or the perspective.

On FIG. 6, break lines on only two edges would have left the vertical edges reading as the real ends of the shell wall, which is a statement about the extent of the shell and about where the indicator sits along it. The disclosure gives neither. Breaking all four edges says only that the view is a fragment, which is what the sheet is.

The indefinite rib was worth correcting because the mating channel paragraph is where the engagement is first described, and an unnumbered indefinite rib invites the reading that some rib other than 62 could do the registering. The part now carries the same designation there as in the claims, the Summary and the following section.
Two edits lengthened their files slightly and none approached the ceiling, so no compensating compression was needed and no numeral, leader target or curve content moved.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is nothing to cite, nothing to distinguish and no reference vocabulary to avoid; the Background carries no citation and there is no characterisation for a citation review to test. The Background states the problem in the inventor's own terms: the temperature spread that results when a refrigerant mass is laid against a payload, the dependence of any imposed circulation path on an alignment the packer must produce by hand, the condensate left by repeated opening of a reusable carrier, and the erasure of an excursion once the refrigerant recovers. Each states the technical problem that a specific claimed feature solves, and the solution appears in the Detailed Description in the same words the claims use, which is what a later argument would be built from. The distinguishing weight remains on lid-driven registration: the closing travel of the lid shifting the thermal module until the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, so the alignment the passive circulation path depends on is produced by an act the packer cannot skip. The secondary positions are the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator, which reports the state of the refrigerant itself and survives its recovery, and the wick in a condensate channel serviced by a pull tab without opening or removing a cassette. This turn corrected three drawing citations, one indefinite part reference and two figure-brief statements, so no claim scope moved. As the drafting brief records, no prior-art search was run, so the claims have never been measured against a real reference and a search should be run before filing.

invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

1	# Previous review - verdict: fail
2	
3	Reviewed input/disclosure.md, input/conversation.md (one USER passage; the single YOU passage is context only), input/brief.md (formalities only), draft sections 01–10, draft/numerals.md, and all seven figure briefs. A full ledger was built: every limitation of claims 1–20, every numeral in numerals.md, and every structure, relationship, material, position, connection, result, operating condition and variant in the Summary, Detailed Description and figure briefs was traced to an exact affirmative passage of the disclosure, except for the two items reported below.
4	
5	Traced and clean: the shell (floor, side walls, upper edge, ledges), the tray (bottom wall, tray side walls, tray feet standing on the floor, perforations, lower return passage, two side supply passages formed by inward spacing), the module (rigid spacer frame, two opposed cassettes confronting across a central space, downward-opening central inlet, two guide ducts beside the cassettes, peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages, upwardly opening mating channel, resilient feet), the lid (depending indexing rib, compressible gasket sealing after registration, horizontal shift into the registered position, feet pressed against ledges so the module cannot lift away), the complete circulation path, the "free of a fan, a pump and any powered air mover" negative, the condensate channel/wick/pull tab/discharge openings, and the full mechanical exposure indicator chain including the latched exposed position, retention after the cassette cools, manual reset only after opening, and non-control of airflow. Claim 12's progressive-engagement limitation traces to "A compressible lid gasket seals against the upper edge of the shell after registration"; claim 5's removability traces to "conditioned cassettes are fitted to the spacer frame". The optional-feature designation of the channel, wick, pull tab, discharge openings and indicator traces to "The wick and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator are supported optional features."

The circulation path

In the registered position, the outer shell 10, the product tray 20, the thermal module 40 and the insulated lid 60 cooperate to define a circulation path. Air warmed by the goods rises from the product region within the product tray 20 and enters the central inlet opening 48. The rising stream divides along the faces of the first phase-change cassette 44 and the second phase-change cassette 46, giving two cooling streams, and each cooled stream descends through one of the guide ducts 50 beside the phase-change cassettes, leaves the thermal module 40 through the peripheral outlet openings 54, and enters the side supply passage 28 registered beneath that peripheral outlet opening 54. Each descending stream then passes through the perforations 30 in the product tray 20 and returns through the lower return passage 24 beneath the product tray 20.

All three findings are fixed.

- **Condensation mechanism** — the Condensate management paragraph now ends "Condensate present in the guide ducts 50 runs down them and is delivered through the discharge openings 76 into the condensate channel 70 rather than onto the goods." The tray is no longer drawn sitting at floor level, so FIG. 5 agrees with FIG. 1, FIG. 4, the description and claims 1 and 17 about the lower return passage. The trough, wick and pull tab sentences are unchanged.
- **Transport result** — the sentence attributing persistence of the registered overlap to a downward holding force is deleted. The retention paragraph now ends with the supported statement that closure compresses the resilient feet 58 between the spacer frame 42 and the ledges 18 so the module is held down and cannot lift away from the product tray 20 during transport. Claims 2, 14 and 18 are untouched.

input.summary: All three findings are fixed. The Condensate management paragraph now says only that condensate present in the guide ducts runs down them and is delivered through the discharge openings into the condensate channel rather than onto the goods, so the imported account of moist ambient air condensing on the cassettes and duct walls is gone from the Detailed Description while the Background keeps its own prior-art characterisation. The FIG. 5 brief now spaces the thin upright tray wall's lower edge above the top surface of the bottom body, joins the thin horizontal bottom wall to that upright wall above its lower edge with the space beneath it open, and runs the vertical space on down past that lower edge to the bottom body, so the tray is no longer drawn at floor level and FIG. 5 agrees with FIG. 1, FIG. 4, the description and claims 1 and 17. The sentence attributing persistence of the registered overlap to a downward holding force from the resilient feet is deleted, leaving the supported retention statement that closes the paragraph. Numerals across the seven sheets still match the 31 table entries in both directions, every brief is within the length limit with FIG. 4 longest at 2798 characters, and no placeholder or em dash remains.
reasoning: The condensation clause was the clearest kind of defect to cure: invention text borrowing a mechanism from my own Background. Prior-art framing can say where condensate comes from in existing carriers, but the Detailed Description may only say what the inventor said, which is that openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts discharge condensate into the channel. The replacement sentence keeps the disclosed route and the disclosed benefit of keeping water off the goods, and drops the origin and the surfaces.

That deletion costs nothing in support. Claims 7 and 16 recite discharge openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts discharging condensate into the channel, and the paragraph still describes exactly that.

The FIG. 5 contradiction was geometric and would have produced a wrong sheet: joining the tray bottom wall at the lower end of the upright wall while bounding the vertical space down to the floor puts the tray on the floor and erases the lower return passage the perforations open into. Spacing the wall's lower edge above the bottom body, attaching the bottom wall above that edge, and letting the vertical space continue past it restores the tray height that FIG. 1 and FIG. 4 show and that claim 1 requires, without adding any contact or seal.

On the transport sentence, the disclosure supports the module being held down so it cannot lift away, which the preceding sentence already states. Persistence of the horizontal overlap through the journey is a different result, and a downward clamp is not the disclosed means of resisting horizontal movement, so the sentence asserted both an untraced result and an untraced mechanism. Deleting it leaves the retention effect intact and does not touch claims 2, 14 or 18.

No compensating compression was needed: the two description edits shortened their paragraphs, and FIG. 5 grew only to 2677 characters, well inside the limit. No numeral, leader target or curve content moved.

draft/08-detailed-description.md, Registration and retention by the lid: the sentence 'The resilient feet 58 maintain a downward holding force during transport, so the registered overlap between the peripheral outlet openings 54 and the side supply passages 28 that was established at closure persists through the journey.' is deleted.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is nothing to cite, nothing to distinguish and no reference vocabulary to avoid; the Background carries no citation and there is no characterisation for a citation review to test. The Background states the problem in the inventor's own terms: the temperature spread that results when a refrigerant mass is laid against a payload, the dependence of any imposed circulation path on an alignment the packer must produce by hand, the condensate left by repeated opening of a reusable carrier, and the erasure of an excursion once the refrigerant recovers. This turn tightened the boundary between that framing and the invention text by removing a condensation mechanism the Detailed Description had borrowed from it, which strengthens rather than weakens the position: the Background still names the problem, and the description now claims only the disclosed solution. The distinguishing weight remains on lid-driven registration, the closing travel of the lid shifting the thermal module until the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, so the alignment the passive circulation path depends on is produced by an act the packer cannot skip. The secondary positions are the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator, which reports the state of the refrigerant itself and survives its recovery, and the wick in a condensate channel serviced by a pull tab without opening or removing a cassette. No claim scope moved. As the drafting brief records, no prior-art search was run, so the claims have never been measured against a real reference and a search should be run before filing.

The circulation path

lines: This sequence addresses the practical problem that the circulation path depends on an alignment which a person packing quickly at a bench cannot be relied upon to produce. The thermal module 40 is placed in the outer shell 10 above the product tray 20, and the registration is completed by the closing of the lid. The alignment on which the circulation path depends is therefore created by an act the packer cannot omit, because a carrier that is not closed does not ship. The compressible lid gasket 64 bears against the upper edge of the outer shell 10 and is compressed only at the end of the closing travel, after the depending indexing rib 62 has completed registration, so that the carrier cannot be sealed shut around a thermal module 40 that is still out of position.

The same closing movement retains the thermal module 40. Ledges 18 of the outer shell 10 lie beneath the resilient feet 58 of the spacer frame 42, one such ledge 18 and one such resilient foot 58 being seen in FIG. 3, and closure of the insulated lid 60 presses the resilient feet 58 against the ledges 18. Closure of the insulated lid 60 compresses the resilient feet 58 between the spacer frame 42 and the ledges 18, so that the thermal module 40 is held down and cannot lift away from the product tray 20 during transport.
The circulation path

In the registered position, the outer shell 10, the product tray 20, the thermal module 40 and the insulated lid 60 cooperate to define a circulation path. Air warmed by the goods rises from the product region within the product tray 20 and enters the central inlet opening 48. The rising stream divides along the faces of the first phase-change cassette 44 and the second phase-change cassette 46, giving two cooling streams, and each cooled stream descends through one of the guide ducts 50 beside the phase-change cassettes, leaves the thermal module 40 through the peripheral outlet openings 54, and enters the side supply passage 28 registered beneath that peripheral outlet opening 54. Each descending stream then passes through the perforations 30 in the product tray 20 and returns through the lower return passage 24 beneath the product tray 20.

Two thick hatched upright wall bodies joined by a thick hatched bottom form a container open at top: the sectioned outer shell 10, its bottom the floor 12. Each wall body carries an inward-projecting block below its top end. A thick hatched slab across both top ends is the insulated lid 60, closed, a narrow rib projecting down inboard of the left end and a compressible body between slab and each end.

Within it, a sectioned open-top box of thin hatched walls and bottom is the product tray 20, held above the floor 12 by short hatched blocks, two appearing here, shown schematically, the tray feet 22. Its walls stand clear of the wall bodies, leaving an open vertical gap each side, with small openings through the tray where each gap meets the space beneath the tray. One shallow trough runs around the tray, cut at both gap feet so it appears at each, one elongated absorbent body in it appearing in both, a narrow strip at one end of the right-hand appearance.

Above the tray, below the lid 60, an elongated hatched body in section is the thermal module 40, open downward at its centre, holding two upright hatched blocks, shown schematically, spaced apart. An open vertical channel runs down outboard of each block, opening through the body's outboard side below the projecting block and above the gap, and at its downward lower end over the trough. Above the upper edges of the blocks the central space and both channels are continuous across the top of the body, so the stream entering at the centre divides into the two channels. A small block is flattened between a down-facing outboard surface of the body and each projecting block, the body continuing down inboard. A groove opening upward in the top surface takes the rib's lower end.

and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than

# FIG. 1

Schematic vertical section of an assembled carrier, on a plane cutting both upright blocks in the module body and its top groove. Plain black line work, hatching on cut material, inside the drawing area.

Two thick hatched upright wall bodies joined by a thick hatched bottom form a container open at top: the sectioned outer shell 10, its bottom the floor 12. Each wall body carries an inward-projecting block below its top. A thick hatched slab across both top ends is the insulated lid 60, closed, a narrow rib projecting down inboard of the left end and a compressible body between slab and each end.

Within it, a sectioned open-top box of thin hatched walls and bottom is the product tray 20, held above the floor 12 by short hatched blocks, two appearing here, shown schematically, the tray feet 22. Its walls stand clear of the wall bodies, leaving an open vertical gap each side, with small openings through the tray where each gap meets the space beneath. One shallow trough runs around the tray, cut at both gaps so it appears at each, one elongated absorbent body appearing in both, a narrow strip at one end of the right-hand appearance.

Above the tray, below the lid 60, an elongated hatched body in section is the thermal module 40, open downward at its centre, holding two upright hatched blocks, shown schematically, spaced apart. An open vertical channel runs down outboard of each block, opening through the body's outboard side below the projecting block and above the gap, and at its downward lower end over the trough. Above the upper edges of the blocks the central space and both channels are continuous across the top of the body, so the stream entering at the centre divides into both channels. A small block is flattened between a down-facing outboard surface of the body and each projecting block, the body continuing down inboard. A groove opening upward in the top surface takes the rib's lower end.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is nothing to cite, nothing to distinguish and no reference vocabulary to avoid; the Background carries no citation and there is no characterisation for a citation review to test. The Background states the problem in the inventor's own terms: the temperature spread that results when a refrigerant mass is laid against a payload, the dependence of any imposed circulation path on an alignment the packer must produce by hand, the condensate left by repeated opening of a reusable carrier, and the erasure of an excursion once the refrigerant recovers. Each states the technical problem that a specific claimed feature solves, and the solution appears in the Detailed Description in the same words the claims use, which is what a later argument would be built from. The distinguishing weight remains on lid-driven registration: the closing travel of the lid shifting the thermal module until the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, so the alignment the passive circulation path depends on is produced by an act the packer cannot skip. The secondary positions are the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator, which reports the state of the refrigerant itself and survives its recovery, and the wick in a condensate channel serviced by a pull tab without opening or removing a cassette. This turn only deleted untraced geometry from two figure briefs, so no claim scope moved and the claims still rest on the disclosed division along the cassette faces and descent through the guide ducts. As the drafting brief records, no prior-art search was run, so the claims have never been measured against a real reference and a search should be run before filing.

The current draft did not pass the automatic filing gate.

Read review/previous-qa.md, then fix every listed mechanical check and every independently
verified finding. Do not argue with a finding in the structured response. If wording triggered a
false positive, make the draft unambiguous enough that the check passes without changing the
invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

Leave no note, placeholder, question, or instruction for a person. Return the structured answer
with `action` set to "revised" and `questions` as an empty array.

# FIG. 2

Perspective view of the thermal module alone, seen from above and in front so the open top, the near long side wall and the right short end wall are visible. Plain black line work on white, no hatching, all inside the drawing area.

The main body is a rectangular open frame, shown schematically, with near and far long side walls, left and right short end walls and a bottom panel joining them, its top open. This frame is the spacer frame 42; with the two slabs it holds it is the thermal module 40.

Two flat rectangular slabs stand upright inside the frame, parallel to the long side walls, their extent along the frame shown schematically. They are spaced apart across the frame depth, leaving an open central gap between their confronting broad faces, and each is spaced from the adjacent long side wall, leaving an open vertical channel between slab and wall. The slab nearer the front is the first phase-change cassette 44, the slab nearer the back the second phase-change cassette 46, each a plain closed box, shown schematically.

In the bottom panel, within the open central gap between the slabs, a rectangular through opening is drawn, so the viewer looks down through the panel there. This opening is the central inlet opening 48.

A further through opening passes down through the bottom panel at the foot of the channel beside each slab, so the viewer looks down through the panel there and each channel is open at its lower end.

an insulated outer shell having a floor, side walls and an upper edge;

The FIG. 2 outward step is now placed above the peripheral outlet opening 54 rather than on the lower part of each long side wall, so it no longer occupies the same height band as that port and no longer contradicts FIG. 1 and FIG. 3, which put the resilient feet and shell ledges in the upper region next to the closed lid while the outlet belongs to the lower FIG. 4 region. reasoning: The FIG. 2 conflict was a real cross-view contradiction about one part. FIG. 1 encloses the feet and ledges in the upper left curve that FIG. 3 enlarges, and puts the outboard channel opening in the lower left curve that FIG. 4 enlarges, so the feet sit well above the outlet. Saying the step is above the peripheral outlet opening ties the two features together by a relationship the other sheets already establish, rather than by a new height that no source gives, and it keeps the step from being drawn across the port it would otherwise obstruct.

I anchored the step to the outlet opening rather than to the frame's top or bottom because that is the relationship the drawing set already fixes, and because the disclosure relates the feet only to the shell ledges and the outlets only to the side supply passages. An absolute height would have been a new assertion; a relative order that FIG. 1 and FIG. 3 already imply is not.

Claim 14 said the module is held down against the product tray, which reads as the module bearing on the tray. The disclosure says only that it cannot lift away from the tray, and claim 2, claim 18 and the description all use that formulation. Conforming claim 14 removes a relationship the source never states and makes one element read the same way across the whole claim set. It narrows nothing, since bearing on the tray was never the disclosed retention effect.
Nothing else moved. The step edit lengthened FIG. 2 only slightly and it remains inside the limit, no numeral or leader target changed, and the claim edit touched a single clause.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is nothing to cite, nothing to distinguish and no reference vocabulary to avoid; the Background carries no citation and there is no characterisation for a citation review to test. The Background states the problem in the inventor's own terms: the temperature spread that results when a refrigerant mass is laid against a payload, the dependence of any imposed circulation path on an alignment the packer must produce by hand, the condensate left by repeated opening of a reusable carrier, and the erasure of an excursion once the refrigerant recovers. Each states the technical problem that a specific claimed feature solves, and the solution appears in the Detailed Description in the same words the claims use, which is what a later argument would be built from. The distinguishing weight remains on lid-driven registration: the closing travel of the lid shifting the thermal module until the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, so the alignment the passive circulation path depends on is produced by an act the packer cannot skip. The secondary positions are the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator, which reports the state of the refrigerant itself and survives its recovery, and the wick in a condensate channel serviced by a pull tab without opening or removing a cassette. This turn conformed one dependent claim to the disclosed retention relationship and corrected one figure brief, so no independent claim scope moved. As the drafting brief records, no prior-art search was run, so the claims have never been measured against a real reference and a search should be run before filing.

A thick hatched upright insulating wall body occupies the left portion of the drawing area and runs the full height of the fragment. Its inner surface faces right. The fragment is taken below the level of the inward projections of the wall bodies.

The finding is fixed in the two figure briefs.

- `figures/FIG-2.md` — the step paragraph now reads "Each long side wall carries an outward step, shown schematically, the step having a downwardly facing surface outboard of the frame." The elevation relationship to the peripheral outlet opening 54 is gone. The step, its downwardly facing outboard surface, the schematic blocks and numeral 58 all remain, since the disclosure affirmatively gives resilient feet of the spacer frame pressed against ledges of the shell.
- `figures/FIG-4.md` — "The fragment is taken below the level of the inward projections of the wall bodies." is replaced by "The inward projections of the wall bodies lie outside this fragment." That still tells the renderer no ledge appears in this view, stated positively as a view-scope fact, without asserting a direction relative to the outlet port.

Both edits shortened their briefs, so nothing needed compensating compression. No file in `draft/` changed: the claims, the Detailed Description, the Brief Description and the numeral table never recited this relationship, and claim 2 still says only that the outer shell has ledges beneath the resilient feet. Numeral coverage still matches the 31 table entries exactly in both directions, all seven briefs are within the length limit with FIG. 2 longest at 2747 characters, and no placeholder or em dash remains.

input.summary: The finding is fixed in the two figure briefs. FIG. 2 no longer places the resilient-foot step above the peripheral outlet opening 54, reading now that each long side wall carries an outward step, shown schematically, having a downwardly facing surface outboard of the frame. FIG. 4 no longer says its fragment is taken below the level of the inward projections; it now states positively that the inward projections of the wall bodies lie outside this fragment, which still tells the renderer no ledge appears in the view without asserting a direction relative to the outlet port. The step, its outboard bearing surface, the schematic blocks, numeral 58 and the schematic ledge elsewhere all remain, because the disclosure gives resilient feet of the spacer frame pressed against ledges of the shell. No file in draft/ changed, both edits shortened their briefs, numeral coverage still matches the 31 table entries exactly in both directions, and all seven briefs are within the length limit with FIG. 2 longest at 2747 characters.
reasoning: The elevation statement was mine from the previous round, added to separate the step from the outlet port after a cross-view conflict, and it solved that conflict by asserting something the inventor never said. The disclosure ties the feet to the ledges and the outlets to the side supply passages and never relates the two, so fixing one above the other decides whether the ledge stands in the path the port discharges into. That is flow-boundary substance, not an outline choice, and the schematic tag does not reach it.

Removing it does not reopen the earlier conflict, because the sheets no longer make competing claims about that height at all: FIG. 2 simply gives the frame an outward step with a downwardly facing outboard surface, and FIG. 1 and FIG. 3 continue to show a foot flattened between such a surface and a ledge top, which is the disclosed relationship.

For FIG. 4 I used a positive view-scope sentence rather than the earlier directional one. Saying the projections lie outside this fragment gives the renderer the same practical instruction, that no ledge is drawn here, while stating a fact about the view instead of a fact about the invention, and it avoids the negative linework phrasing that failed an earlier gate.

I changed nothing in draft/. Claim 2 recites only that the outer shell has ledges beneath the resilient feet, and neither the description nor the Brief Description recites any relationship to the outlets, so the text was already correct and adding to it to justify a drawing would invert the authority order.
Both edits are deletions or substitutions that shortened their files, so no compensating compression was needed and no numeral, leader target or curve content moved.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is nothing to cite, nothing to distinguish and no reference vocabulary to avoid; the Background carries no citation and there is no characterisation for a citation review to test. The Background states the problem in the inventor's own terms: the temperature spread that results when a refrigerant mass is laid against a payload, the dependence of any imposed circulation path on an alignment the packer must produce by hand, the condensate left by repeated opening of a reusable carrier, and the erasure of an excursion once the refrigerant recovers. Each states the technical problem that a specific claimed feature solves, and the solution appears in the Detailed Description in the same words the claims use, which is what a later argument would be built from. The distinguishing weight remains on lid-driven registration: the closing travel of the lid shifting the thermal module until the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, so the alignment the passive circulation path depends on is produced by an act the packer cannot skip. The secondary positions are the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator, which reports the state of the refrigerant itself and survives its recovery, and the wick in a condensate channel serviced by a pull tab without opening or removing a cassette. This turn removed one untraced elevation relationship from two figure briefs, so no claim scope moved. As the drafting brief records, no prior-art search was run, so the claims have never been measured against a real reference and a search should be run before filing.

content:
The current draft did not pass the automatic filing gate.

Read review/previous-qa.md, then fix every listed mechanical check and every independently
verified finding. Do not argue with a finding in the structured response. If wording triggered a
false positive, make the draft unambiguous enough that the check passes without changing the
invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

Leave no note, placeholder, question, or instruction for a person. Return the structured answer
with `action` set to "revised" and `questions` as an empty array.

The condensate trough is now located outboard of the thin upright wall and below the discharge opening 76, so it stays under the duct end without relying on the passage reaching the floor; the trough, wick and pull tab sentences are otherwise unchanged. reasoning: Carrying the vertical space down to the bottom body was the defect, because the tray stands on its feet: once the passage passes below the tray bottom wall, the side supply passage and the lower return passage are open to each other around the tray, and the perforations stop being the boundary the claims rely on. Stopping the space at the tray and saying in the brief that the small openings are the only drawn connection restores the single route without adding any seal, skirt or contact.

I phrased that as the only connection drawn, which is a statement about this view rather than an assertion that no other route could exist in any embodiment. It gives the renderer the boundary it needs and keeps the brief from making a claim about the invention that the disclosure does not make.

The trough needed a new anchor once the passage no longer reached the floor. Outboard of the thin upright wall and below the discharge opening 76 keeps it where the disclosure puts it, under the openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts that discharge condensate into the channel, and it relates the trough to parts that are actually in this fragment.

FIG. 1 and FIG. 4 were already correct and were left alone: FIG. 1 has small openings through the tray where each gap meets the space beneath, and FIG. 4 identifies the perforations 30 as the connection. Correcting the one brief that disagreed was the right direction rather than propagating its geometry.

Nothing in draft/ moved. The description and claims already recite the perforated route, so the text was the authority the drawing had to conform to, not the other way round. FIG. 5 grew slightly to 2595 characters, well inside the limit, so no compensating compression was needed and no numeral or leader target changed.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is nothing to cite, nothing to distinguish and no reference vocabulary to avoid; the Background carries no citation and there is no characterisation for a citation review to test. The Background states the problem in the inventor's own terms: the temperature spread that results when a refrigerant mass is laid against a payload, the dependence of any imposed circulation path on an alignment the packer must produce by hand, the condensate left by repeated opening of a reusable carrier, and the erasure of an excursion once the refrigerant recovers. Each states the technical problem that a specific claimed feature solves, and the solution appears in the Detailed Description in the same words the claims use, which is what a later argument would be built from. The distinguishing weight remains on lid-driven registration: the closing travel of the lid shifting the thermal module until the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, so the alignment the passive circulation path depends on is produced by an act the packer cannot skip. This turn restores the drawing support for the second half of that path, the descent through the side supply passage and out through the perforations into the lower return passage, which claims 1, 13 and 17 all recite. The secondary positions are the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator, which reports the state of the refrigerant itself and survives its recovery, and the wick in a condensate channel serviced by a pull tab without opening or removing a cassette. No claim scope moved. As the drafting brief records, no prior-art search was run, so the claims have never been measured against a real reference and a search should be run before filing.

# FIG. 5

Enlarged view of the condensate channel region of FIG. 1 enclosed by the broken-line curve there designated FIG. 5, seen horizontally in section on the right side of the carrier. Plain black line work on white, diagonal section hatching on cut material. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the margins.

A thick hatched upright insulating wall body occupies the right portion of the drawing area, running from the upper part of the fragment down to a thick hatched horizontal bottom body that occupies the lower part and extends leftward.

In the upper left part of the drawing area, a hatched portion of the module body is drawn in section. An open vertical channel passes down through this module body, bounded by hatched material to its left and right. This channel is one of the guide ducts 50. At the lower end of the channel, an opening passes through the downwardly facing bottom surface of the module body. This opening is one of the discharge openings 76.

Below the module body, a thin hatched upright wall is drawn in section, spaced to the left of the inner surface of the upright wall body, and a thin hatched horizontal bottom wall joined to the lower end of that upright wall and extending leftward, the space beneath that bottom wall being open. A series of small openings passes through the product tray where that upright wall meets that bottom wall, as in FIG. 1 and FIG. 4. An open vertical space runs down between the upright wall body and the thin wall, so that the downward opening in the module body stands above that space, the small openings through the product tray being the only connection drawn between that space and the space beneath the bottom wall.

In the upwardly facing top surface of the horizontal bottom body, outboard of the thin upright wall and below the discharge opening 76, a shallow upwardly open trough is drawn in section, wider than it is deep. This trough is the condensate channel 70.

An elongated body of absorbent material lies in the trough, shown schematically. This body is the absorbent wick 72. A narrow strip, shown schematically, extends from one end of the absorbent body, its free end clear of the absorbent body. This strip is the pull tab 74.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 50: inside the open vertical channel in the module body.
- 70: inside the trough, clear of the absorbent body.
- 72: well inside the elongated absorbent body lying in the trough.
- 74: well inside the narrow strip extending from the absorbent body.
- 76: on the opening through the bottom surface of the module body.

content.text:
The finding is fixed in `figures/FIG-5.md` alone, by deletion.

- The geometry paragraph now ends "An open vertical space runs down between the upright wall body and the thin wall, so that the downward opening in the module body stands above that space." The clause calling the tray perforations the only connection between that space and the space beneath the tray bottom wall is gone.

Everything else in that brief is untouched: the tray side wall joined at its lower end to the tray bottom wall with the space beneath open, the series of small openings through the product tray where the two meet, the trough outboard of the thin upright wall and below the discharge opening 76, the wick, the pull tab and the numeral list. FIG. 1 and FIG. 4 were already free of any exclusivity statement and were left as they are, so the three briefs now agree with each other, with the Detailed Description and with claims 1, 13 and 17, all of which recite the path through the perforations without saying it is the sole route.

The deletion shortened the brief to 2461 characters. Numeral coverage still matches the 31 table entries exactly in both directions, all seven briefs are within the length limit, and no placeholder or em dash remains. No file in `draft/` changed.

input.summary: The finding is fixed by deleting one clause from figures/FIG-5.md. The geometry paragraph now ends with the open vertical space running down between the shell wall body and the thin tray wall so that the downward opening in the module body stands above that space, and no longer calls the tray perforations the only connection between that space and the space beneath the tray bottom wall. Everything else in the brief is untouched, including the tray wall joined to the tray bottom wall with the space beneath open, the small openings through the product tray where they meet, the trough outboard of the thin upright wall and below the discharge opening 76, the wick, the pull tab and the numeral list. FIG. 1 and FIG. 4 already carried no exclusivity statement and were left alone, so the three briefs now agree with each other, with the Detailed Description and with claims 1, 13 and 17. No file in draft/ changed, the brief shortened to 2461 characters, numeral coverage still matches the 31 table entries exactly in both directions, and no placeholder or em dash remains.
reasoning: The exclusivity clause was mine, added last round to keep the passage from bypassing the perforations, and it went wrong in two ways at once. The disclosure recites the air's route through the perforations but never says that is the only route, and the tray is expressly suspended above the floor on feet, so the region beneath it is open. Saying the perforations are the sole connection asserts a flow boundary the inventor did not give, and a schematic label cannot carry that kind of statement.

It was also unachievable from the geometry in the same brief: with the tray wall ending at the tray bottom wall, the space beneath that wall open, and the trough in the floor outboard of the tray wall, the two spaces necessarily meet below the tray wall's lower edge. A brief that specifies geometry and then denies its consequence cannot be rendered faithfully either way.

Deleting the clause is enough because the disclosed route is still drawn. The small openings through the product tray where the upright wall meets the bottom wall remain in FIG. 5, FIG. 4 still says the side supply passage opens through them into the space beneath the bottom wall, and FIG. 1 still shows small openings where each gap meets the space beneath. The claims recite the path in order without exclusivity, so text and drawings now say the same thing.
I left FIG. 1, FIG. 4 and every file in draft/ untouched. They were already correct, and editing them to accommodate a figure statement would invert the authority order.
The edit was subtractive, so nothing needed compensating compression and no numeral, leader target or curve content moved.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is nothing to cite, nothing to distinguish and no reference vocabulary to avoid; the Background carries no citation and there is no characterisation for a citation review to test. The Background states the problem in the inventor's own terms: the temperature spread that results when a refrigerant mass is laid against a payload, the dependence of any imposed circulation path on an alignment the packer must produce by hand, the condensate left by repeated opening of a reusable carrier, and the erasure of an excursion once the refrigerant recovers. Each states the technical problem that a specific claimed feature solves, and the solution appears in the Detailed Description in the same words the claims use, which is what a later argument would be built from. The distinguishing weight remains on lid-driven registration: the closing travel of the lid shifting the thermal module until the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages, so the alignment the passive circulation path depends on is produced by an act the packer cannot skip. The secondary positions are the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator, which reports the state of the refrigerant itself and survives its recovery, and the wick in a condensate channel serviced by a pull tab without opening or removing a cassette. This turn deleted one untraced clause from a figure brief, so no claim scope moved and the claimed circulation path is unchanged. As the drafting brief records, no prior-art search was run, so the claims have never been measured against a real reference and a search should be run before filing.

content:
The current draft did not pass the automatic filing gate.

Read review/previous-qa.md, then fix every listed mechanical check and every independently
verified finding. Do not argue with a finding in the structured response. If wording triggered a
false positive, make the draft unambiguous enough that the check passes without changing the
invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

Leave no note, placeholder, question, or instruction for a person. Return the structured answer
with `action` set to "revised" and `questions` as an empty array.

3	I traced every claim limitation, every numbered part (10, 12, 14, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 30, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48, 50, 54, 56, 58, 60, 62, 64, 70, 72, 74, 76, 80, 82, 84, 86, 100), and every structure, relationship, result, material, position, connection and variant in draft/04 through draft/10 and in the seven figure briefs back to the disclosure and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which is verbatim identical to input/disclosure.md; the only other conversation turn is labelled YOU and is therefore not inventor support).
4	
5	The substantive ledger is essentially clean. Every claim limitation traces to an affirmative source passage: the shell/tray/module/lid architecture, the tray feet and lower return passage, the inward-spaced tray walls and two side supply passages, the rigid spacer frame with two opposed cassettes, the central inlet opening, the two downward guide ducts beside the cassettes, the peripheral outlet openings aligned with (and overlapping) the side supply passages, the full circulation path, the "no fan, pump or powered air mover" negative limitation, the depending indexing rib entering the mating channel and shifting the module into the registered position, the gasket sealing after registration (which is the affirmative basis for claim 12's "spaced above the upper edge ... remaining closing travel"), the resilient feet pressed against ledges, the condensate channel/wick/pull tab/discharge openings, and the whole mechanical exposure indicator chain including the latched exposed position, manual reset only after opening, and the "does not control airflow" limitation. The method claims 17-20 track the source's "For use" paragraph. Title, "Not applicable" cross-reference and government-support statements match input/brief.md, which I used only for those formalities.
6	
7	Internal consistency checks pass: the numeral table matches every numeral used in the description and in the figure briefs with no numeral bearing two meanings and no numeral orphaned from the drawings; the Brief Description of each figure matches its brief; the three broken-line enlargement curves carry the same designations "FIG. 3", "FIG. 4" and "FIG. 5" in FIG-1.md, in the Brief Description, and in the headings of FIG-3.md, FIG-4.md and FIG-5.md; the section line is designated "7-7" identically in FIG-6.md (repeated designation 7 at both arrow ends), in FIG-7.md, and in the Brief Description, and the arrow direction in FIG. 6 is geometrically consistent with FIG. 7 showing the shell's outer surface at page-left. FIG. 1's stated section plane (transverse to the cassettes, through the mating channel) is consistent with FIG. 2's placement of the mating channel on the top edge of the near long side wall and with the left/right assignment of the FIG. 3, FIG. 4 and FIG. 5 fragments. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains, and the description contains no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language that would push a renderer's shape choice into the application text.
8	
9	I judged the following as entailed by the source rather than untraced, and did not report them: the cassettes described as "upright" and confronting across a central space (entailed by "two opposed phase-change cassettes" plus air that "divides along faces of the cassettes, descends through the guide ducts"); the mating channel "opens upward at a top region" (entailed by a depending rib on the lid entering it from above); the cassettes being removable from the frame (entailed by "conditioned cassettes are fitted to the spacer frame"); the perforations drawn where the tray side wall meets the tray bottom wall (the only position consistent with the disclosed side-supply-passage-to-return-passage route); the condensate trough drawn in the shell floor outboard of the tray wall (entailed by "around the product tray", discharge from the guide-duct lower ends, and the pull tab remaining accessible when the tray is removed); the indicator body and horizontal stem drawn in a side wall (entailed by "The shell includes a mechanical exposure indicator visible from outside"); and the flat, upwardly facing ledge surface and the flattened gasket and foot contacts (all disclosed as "seals against the upper edge" and "presses resilient feet ... against ledges").
